Needless to say that the social and cultural characteristics of the university, as well as scientific and research activities are in line with the grand plans of the Islamic Republic of Iran in achieving both spiritual and physical development. Therefore, the Vice-President for Socio-Cultural Affairs of the Ferdowsi University of Mashhad tries to prepare the required frameworks and preparations for social and cultural development of all university members (students, faculty and staff) with the help of its experienced and knowledgeable academics. In this regard, the university students who are the largest group of academic members of the university and the future generation of Iran, have always had the most prominent role in the cultural and social programs of the university and they have had great achievements in these affairs. In recent years, the Ferdowsi University of Mashhad has always been a leading model in terms of being a cultural and academic community. Although the Vice-President for Socio-Cultural Affairs has followed wonderful strategies to train skilled experts in social and cultural aspects of academic life, it is still behind its ideal status. Major Goals Encouraging community participation, social discipline, and improvement of mental and social health and vitality Expanding and deepening constructive interactions and synergy with scientific, cultural, social, sports and economic centers at national and international levels Enhancing students and graduates’ sense of commitment to the university Developing and upgrading the infrastructure and cultural, physical, and technological areas in the university. Activities The activities of this office can be divided into three general categories: Supervision, support and organization of university students’ associations: To supervise, support and organize students’ associations such as art and culture centers, science foundations (there are more than ninety specialized foundations and twenty interdisciplinary centers at FUM), Basij and Islamic associations (the Islamic University Students’ Association, Islamic Society of Students, and Islamic Association of Neo-thinker Students) and publications (more than 80 students publications) Supervision, support and organization of staff and professors’ associations Additional activities are related to pilgrimage center, movies center, recreational services, campus galleries, audio-visual center, reunion, and camps centers. Responsibilities Undertaking cultural, political and social programs in the university Collaborating with cultural institutions and revolutionary centers, especially those that are present at the university Publishing newsletters or cultural journals at the university level Providing facilities for cultural activities of students, staff, and faculty members Organizing some recreational, scientific, research, sports and arts programs Encouraging the students to participate in arts activities, tours and festivals Performing art festivals as well as organizing exhibitions Establishing university students’ associations in various cultural, arts and social fields based on the university’ laws and regulations Planning various scientific and cultural excursions Planning competitions in science and arts More Head of the Vice President for Socio-Cultural and Student Affairs Dr. Abulfazl Ghaffari Assistant Professor Faculty of Education and Psychology ghaffari@um.ac.ir +985138802512 Map of the Vice President for Socio-Cultural and Student Affairs Policies, rules and governance Contact Information Iran, Mashhad, Azadi Square, Ferdowsi University of Mashhad Administrative Affairs, 3 th Floor, Vice President for Research And Technology Phone: +9851 38806472-6472 Fax: +985138807071 Postal code: 9177948974 Top

Since 2007 the mission of the college is divided into two parts : Main mission: Managing, planning and holding a higher education open system . Sub-mission: Conducting a variety of training services needed by the society . The College pursues the following goals To improve the level of education and culture To create appropriate basis for increasing access to higher education To expand and develop professional and practical environment in the higher education system To reduce the social demand for official education in higher education institutions To provide ongoing training courses for graduates of universities and higher education institutions. Types of Training A. Open Higher Education The mission of Open Higher Education covers curriculum planning and implementation of courses that are required for different sectors of the society, such as organizations, public and private institutions, and industries. Regardless of the existing obstacles such as the entrance exam, the Open Higher Education System facilitates everyone’s access to the acquisition of academic knowledge. In such an educational system, syllabi are designed according to the needs of the learners. B. Minor Courses Minor courses are the ones which talented students of the second year onwards in the Bachelor’s program can participate in under special conditions such as having good GPA score. Passing 21 to 25 units of specialized courses in another Bachelor’s majors offered at Ferdowsi University of Mashhad through these courses, students will become familiar with other majors and specialties that are of their interest. C. Training and entrepreneurial courses The training and entrepreneurial courses are the ones in which students of a particular major will be well acquainted with the practical issues of their profession that are not covered in the framework of the Bachelor’s program. These courses are concerned with practical issues, workshops, and executive projects. Training and entrepreneurial courses can also be up to about 24 units. All Ferdowsi University students (undergraduate and postgraduate) can participate in the training and entrepreneurial courses supervised by the College of Ferdowsi University of Mashhad and are held by different departments. Training and entrepreneurial courses are between 21 and 24 units. Training courses consist of theoretical discussions and practical activities as well as workshops, fieldwork's, projects and similar other courses. Entrepreneurial courses comprise elective courses. Students of other universities and educational institutions can also enroll in these courses. However, students of Ferdowsi University of Mashhad are in priority. content: Ferdowsi University of Mashhad: Third University in Iran FUM Officials FUM Presidents A word from the President Vice Presidents Vice President for Academic Affairs College of Ferdowsi University of Mashhad Educational Planning and Academic Development Office E-Learning Center Vice President for Socio-Cultural and Student affairs Office of Cultural Affairs and Voluntary Activities Physical Education Administration Office of Health and Welfare Consulting Center for Cultural and Social Empowerment Vice President for Research and Technology Laboratory Network Management Office Office of Industrial Relations Research Management Office Center for Knowledge-based Business Incubator Unites in Humanities Director of FUM President’s Office and Public Relations The History Site Map Strategic Plan FUM Catalogs in Three Languages: English, French and Russian Center for Documents and Scientific Records of Eminent University Figures Information and Communication Technology (ICT) Center Campus Master Plan You are here: About / FUM Officials / Vice Presidents / Vice President for Academic Affairs / E-Learning Center E-Learning Center Nowadays, virtual universities are one of the newest and most efficient forms of distance learning which have played a significant role in education across the world. Virtual universities have changed the concept of traditional classes. Although the activities, which are held in virtual classes are similar to those in traditional classes, the environment is totally different. Ferdowsi University of Mashhad has been one of the pioneers in e-learning. The idea of having virtual classes was put forward in 2001 at Ferdowsi University of Mashhad. The virtual university committee, under the supervision of Information, and Communication Center was formed afterward. This committee aims at developing the basic requirements for establishing a virtual university and its administrative aspects. The result of a research project led to the authorization issued by the Ferdowsi University of Mashhad Board of Directors and the Ministry of Science, Research and Technology to establish one virtual major in the Bachelor’s and nine virtual majors in the Master’s program. This led to the establishment of E-learning Center at Ferdowsi university of Mashhad in 2001. It was established to put more emphasis on e-learning and to develop the idea of electronic education. At the moment, more than 35 undergraduate virtual university subjects are offered in every semester. Summer semester classes are also offered virtually at Ferdowsi University of Mashhad. In addition, the content of more than 100 subjects of Bachelor’s programs is available virtually on e-learning portals. They can either be used as e-learning materials or supplemental online materials to traditional classes. Aims To embed Communication and Information Technology in educational programs to promote the quality of education at Ferdowsi University of Mashhad To enhance the quality of course contents by modern strategies and technologies To help education move beyond time and place limitations To benefit from the knowledge of national and internal professors To offer audience knowledge and skills in a relaxed atmosphere while they are at work or in their family life Activities Offering university courses and majors electronically Offering individual subjects electronically inside and outside the university Preparing course contents based on the SCORM standard Video-recording of class presentations of all faculties to upload to the online e-learning center portal Organizing and supporting conferences, meetings, and seminars electronically Holding and supporting on-line thesis defense sessions in all faculties Collaborating with other universities and institutions to hold virtual supplementary classes Supporting on-line interview and introductory sessions Equipping faculties with facilities available in the e-learning center Holding workshops for faculty members to help them embed information technology in their teaching and enhance educational programs. title: Commencement of the master plan for developing technologies to improve subsurface imaging in the exploration of hydrocarbon resources in the Kopeh Dagh sedimentary basin at Ferdowsi University of Mash :: Ferdowsi University of Mashhad :: Ferdowsi University of Mashhad: Third University in Iran
content: Commencement of the master plan for developing technologies to improve subsurface imaging in the exploration of hydrocarbon resources in the Kopeh Dagh sedimentary basin at Ferdowsi University of Mash :: Ferdowsi University of Mashhad :: Ferdowsi University of Mashhad: Third University in Iran The first phase of the master plan "Development of subsurface imaging improvement technologies in hydrocarbon resource exploration in the Kopeh Dagh sedimentary basin" to create technological capabilities in the oil and gas exploration sector and form an innovation network and business formation in the field of subsurface imaging technologies, has been defined as follows and successfully implemented under difficult sanctions conditions. The technology development roadmap has been developed within the framework of the first package, and accordingly, the research projects of the second package have been defined in two phases and under the title of completing the database data by providing a program to conduct the necessary studies and experiments at three laboratory, semi-industrial and industrial scales. Currently, the first phase of the second package, including 6 projects, has been completed with 100% realization of the anticipated goals. In addition to the universities of Tehran (Institute of Geophysics and Institute of Petroleum), Amirkabir University of Technology, Zanjan Postgraduate Education, and Daqing Normal University, international companies and experts from Russia, Switzerland, Norway, and Mexico have participated in the research project with Ferdowsi University of Mashhad. In the continuation of the implementation of the second phase of the second package of the plan, five project titles with a credit of over 190 billion rials and 2 million and 800 thousand euros have been approved and announced. Considering the university's scientific, administrative capacities, and valuable infrastructure in the fields of reservoir exploration studies, geomechanical studies, and increased recovery, as well as the network of partners formed during the implementation of the plan, Ferdowsi University of Mashhad has announced its readiness to launch a Center for New Exploration Technologies.

title: Joint meeting of the President of Ferdowsi University of Mashhad with Rear Admiral Habibollah Sayyari :: Ferdowsi University of Mashhad :: Ferdowsi University of Mashhad: Third University in Iran
content: Joint meeting of the President of Ferdowsi University of Mashhad with Rear Admiral Habibollah Sayyari :: Ferdowsi University of Mashhad :: Ferdowsi University of Mashhad: Third University in Iran Prof. Javan Jafari, the President of Ferdowsi University of Mashhad, met and discussed with Rear Admiral Habibollah Sayyari, Deputy Coordinator of the General Command of the Islamic Republic of Iran Army on Sunday, June 25, 2025, In this meeting, which was attended by a group of commanders of the Navy, Air Force, Passive Defense, and Rangers of the Islamic Republic of Iran Army, in addition to emphasizing the expansion of cooperation between Ferdowsi University of Mashhad and the executive branches, issues such as utilizing the capacity and capabilities of Ferdowsi University of Mashhad students and the capacities of the Faculty of Engineering in the field of defense production were discussed. Admiral Sayyari, while expressing his pleasure at being at Ferdowsi University of Mashhad and the invitation to participate in the grand program linking epics from Toos to Khorramshahr, considered such programs to be a factor in strengthening religious and national identity. In this regard, he appreciated and thanked the university president.

title: Publication of an article by a faculty member of Ferdowsi University of Mashhad in the prestigious journal Science
content: Publication of an article by a faculty member of Ferdowsi University of Mashhad in the prestigious journal Science Dr. Mansour Aliabadian, a faculty member of the Department of Biology at the Faculty of Science, Ferdowsi University of Mashhad, in collaboration with 44 international researchers, has successfully published an article in the prestigious journal Science. This study examined color variation in four species of light-winged songbirds from the genus wheatears, birds known for their distinctive black and white patterns on the body, throat, and neck feathers. The results of the study show that although the ASIP locus is the primary factor in black pigmentation, each part of the body is affected by different regulatory factors, leading to the emergence of significant color variation. In addition, extensive genetic crossing between different species has caused the transfer of the old white haplotype from the eastern black-eared wheatear (Oenanthe melanoleuca) and the emergence of new mutations with similar patterns in other species. These findings demonstrate that even traits controlled by a single gene can be influenced by complex networks of regulatory factors, thereby playing a crucial role in the processes of evolution and biodiversity. Link to access the article on the Science magazine website: https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.ado8005

title: Publication of a new book by a faculty member of Ferdowsi University of Mashhad by Elsevier International Publishing
content: Publication of a new book by a faculty member of Ferdowsi University of Mashhad by Elsevier International Publishing Dr. Parisa Taheri, a faculty member of the Department of Plant Protection, Faculty of Agriculture, Ferdowsi University of Mashhad, published her new book titled “Environmentally Safe Strategies for Plant Protection Against Biotic and Abiotic Stresses” in the prestigious international publication Elsevier. This book examines and analyzes safe and environmentally friendly mechanisms and methods for protecting plants against biotic and abiotic stresses. Given the increasing global demand for organic food and animal feed, the study and application of natural and biological compounds to promote plant growth and protect agricultural products has become increasingly important. In this work, the role of natural compounds extracted from plants, fungi, and beneficial microorganisms, as well as their metabolites, in strengthening plant defense systems and mitigating environmental stresses has been comprehensively investigated. These compounds can be used as biological control agents with direct or indirect effects within the framework of sustainable and organic agriculture. The aforementioned book, comprising 15 chapters and written in collaboration with prominent researchers from four continents and 12 countries, is a valuable resource for researchers, students, and specialists in the fields of plant medicine, agricultural biotechnology, plant biology, plant physiology, plant microbiology, and environmental sciences.

Although technological changes have brought different types of activities to the center since the past four decades, this center is now more focused on the development and use of ICT in different sectors of the university including educational, research, administrative and executive sections. The Ferdowsi University of Mashhad is one of the few universities where the efficient management of its ICT center has led to the creation of integrated websites and computer networks. These websites and computer networks offer a wide range of services to the students, staff, and faculty members. These services have also been offered to more than 50 universities and institutes of higher education in the form of SADAF (Information Systems of the Ferdowsi University of Mashhad). The Information and Communication Technology (ICT) Center has so far achieved outstanding ranks at the national level leading to the winning of many awards and certificates. All these achievements indicate the quality and productivity of this center and its staff. Missions Monitoring, consulting, designing, managing, running, and supporting projects related to ICT in the Ferdowsi University of Mashhad, Mashhad city, Khorasan Razavi Province, and Iran at its best quality level. Aims of the ICT center Providing the technological basis for designing a technological-based management system Equipping the university with new technologies Doing research in the field of developing, improving, and upgrading systems and networks Managing, running, and ordering ICT projects Providing security and stability in the realm of ICT Teaching ICT related issues Improving the structure as well as internal processes of the ICT Center in order to effectively and dynamically respond to different needs and procedures Fostering the culture of production and the use of open source systems Providing consultation services to other institutions in the field of ICT Map of the Information and Communication Technology (ICT) Center Top

After a long period of being inactive, the center was activated again in 2013. The center for Documents and Scientific Records of Eminent University Figures aims to preserve all documents, including pictures, photos, films, oral or documented memories, and interviews which reflect the University's origins and development, as well as the activities, and achievements of its key figures for future generations. In response to students’ needs, there is a wide range of different specialized services which pursue the following objectives To diagnose and alleviate students’ psychological problems To prevent students’ probable psychological and educational problems in future by holding workshops To reduce students’ problems by providing financial and remedial help To help students make the informed decision about their education, job, and marriage To improve students’ life skills Center’s Responsibilities Providing individual and group counseling Providing consultations on family conflicts Providing consultations for academic perspectives and occupational concerns Providing consultations on marriage Introducing students in-need to different organizations and people who can support them financially Providing counseling services for failed and dropped students to improve their educational status Holding regular meetings with some students’ families- the ones for whom the necessity of communication is felt Holding life skills workshops and other issues related to students’ psychological health Monitoring students' mental health and identifying their potential psychological disorders Center’s Activities The Consulting Center for Cultural and Social Empowerment is active regarding its psychological services as well as social services for clients. content: Ferdowsi University of Mashhad: Third University in Iran FUM Officials FUM Presidents A word from the President Vice Presidents Vice President for Academic Affairs College of Ferdowsi University of Mashhad Educational Planning and Academic Development Office E-Learning Center Vice President for Socio-Cultural and Student affairs Office of Cultural Affairs and Voluntary Activities Physical Education Administration Office of Health and Welfare Consulting Center for Cultural and Social Empowerment Vice President for Research and Technology Laboratory Network Management Office Office of Industrial Relations Research Management Office Center for Knowledge-based Business Incubator Unites in Humanities Director of FUM President’s Office and Public Relations The History Site Map Strategic Plan FUM Catalogs in Three Languages: English, French and Russian Center for Documents and Scientific Records of Eminent University Figures Information and Communication Technology (ICT) Center Campus Master Plan External Links Alzahra University Amirkabir University of Technology Golestan University Shahid Beheshti University Sharif University of Technology Shiraz University Tarbiat Modares University University of Guilan University of Isfahan University of Sistan and Baluchestan University of Tabriz University of Tehran Yazd University You are here: About / The History The History of Ferdowsi University of Mashhad The first proposal for launching the Ferdowsi University of Mashhad was announced concurrently with the establishment of Tehran University in 1934. However, the first step was converting the Higher Institute of Public Health to a Medical Faculty in 1949. Shortly after, the Medical Faculty admitted its first group of medical students, and in December 1949 this institute was officially inaugurated as the first Center for Medical Sciences in the North East of Iran by the Minister of Culture, the late Dr. Zanganeh. Finally in 1956 after the foundation of the facultys of Literature and Theology, the complex was named "Mashhad University". Later on in 1957, the rules and regulations for employment and education of Tehran University were adopted for use in this new university. Since then other faculties have been gradually added to the university based on the local demand. These are the Faculty of Science (1961), the Faculty of Education, the Faculty of Agriculture (1973), the Faculty of Engineering (1975), the Faculty of Economics and Administrative Sciences (1987), the Faculty of Veterinary Medicine (1991), the Faculty of Mathematics (1996), the Faculty of Architecture, the Faculty of Urbanism and Islamic Arts, and the Faculty of Natural Resources and Environment (2001). In 1975 after the separation of the facultys related to the Medical Sciences from the university, the name of the university was changed from "Mashhad University” to "The Ferdowsi University of Mashhad". The Ferdowsi University of Mashhad has now nearly seven decades of brilliant educational, research and cultural history and it is well known among institutes of higher education in Iran. It is currently one of the nation’s top three universities and also the largest center of higher education in the North East of Iran. At present, the Ferdowsi University of Mashhad is composed of 12 facultys , 38 research centers, 7 centers of excellence, 820 faculty members (%50 of whom are professors or associate professors), over 20000 students (9996 undergraduate, 6143 Masters, and 3905 Ph.D. students), and 1050 staff members. Currently, 1279 foreign students are enrolled in different academic programs at the Ferdowsi University of Mashhad. In addition, there are also 187 foreign students who are passing their six-month training courses in language at the International Center for Teaching Persian to Non-Persian Speakers. These students would begin their academic education after they pass this six-month course of study. The transfer time is usually quite short. Otherwise, International flights to Tehran (IKA airport) are more common and there are direct flights from many countries. Mashhad is about 900 km far from Tehran and is accessible via flights, trains, and buses. For taking flights you must switch to THR (Mehrabad) airport. IKA and THR airports are connected by airport taxicabs which service 24/7 (around 18 €; reservation NOT needed). Round trip ticket to Mashhad costs approximately 100 € with the flight time of 1h15. Train tickets are half cheaper but they are usually packed and need to be booked well in advance. Traveling time via railways is about 10 hours. The IKA airport is connected to the train station by airport taxicabs (costs around 20 €; reservation NOT needed). Traveling by public bus is the cheapest but unexpected events may happen (delay, canceling, etc.). Car rental is not that common in Iran; it is expensive and the process is quite complicated. In case you arrive in Tehran, we will arrange to send someone to the airport to help you with airport transfer. When you get to Mashhad, our welcoming committee will pick you up from the airport and accompany you to Ferdowsi University of Mashhad. The same will be arranged for your departure. N.B. local tickets (Tehran-Mashhad-Tehran) cannot be booked via International credit/debit cards and the reservation should be made via national bank cards. Please communicate with us (intr@um.ac.ir) your dates of arrival and departure and we will book your local tickets with the lowest price possible. Please do not hesitate to contact us if you have any further questions or concerns: Email: intr@um.ac.ir Phone:  +985138802415 Fax: +985138836056 Postal Code: 9177948974 Top

Enrollment at the university 2. Referring to the consular affairs center, presenting university’s admission letter and identity documents, filling out the relevant forms and providing the 1st page of the passport 3. Presenting the passport which is valid for a minimum of 8 months and applying for study visa 4. Receiving a number for student visa, referring to the Iranian embassy at your city, receiving student visa and referring to the consular affairs department 5. Applying for the issuance of residency 6. Presenting birth certificate and/or local affidavit, Parents’ identity documents, and passport pages. In case the main caretaker of the family is not the father, it is obligatory to present the letter for determining the caretaker from the office of foreign nationals at provincial governments 7. Presenting passport image photos and filling out the relevant forms 8. Receiving an automation number of residency issuance, delivering all the documents to the consular affairs department and receiving student visa 9. Receiving a registration permission letter from the consular affairs department and presenting it to the university *Female students can only apply for their children and residency would not be issued for their husband and/or other members of their family. Therefore, it is obligatory to present the letter designating that the husband has transferred the custody of the child/children to the female student. This letter has to be approved by the Iranian Ministry of Foreign Affairs. *Male students can apply for the residency of their wife and children, but residency would not be issued for other members of their family. Accordingly, it is obligatory to present the marriage certificate approved by the Iranian Ministry of Foreign Affairs. Also, if the children have been born in Iran, a birth certificate confirming this claim must be presented. Top

Several regional and national authorities participated at this inauguration ceremony. As the first speaker, Dr Alireza Ashuri, the President of Ferdowsi University of Mashhad at the time, said: This pool has been constructed based on updated international standards in order to provide students, employees and faculty members with high-quality sport amenities. Features of the Covered Swimming pool at FUM With a total area of 6350 square meters, the covered swimming pool of Ferdowsi University of Mashhad is considered as one of the biggest pools in Iranian universities and the only standard swimming pool for professional competitions in Khorasan Razavi Province. The complex includes the following facilities: 1) Main pool (50*25 m) for standard professional competitions 2) Children’s pool (6*8 m) 3) Steam sauna, dry sauna, Jacuzzi 4) Hydrotherapy section, fitness room 5) Uncovered cafeteria on the 1st floor and coffee shop on the ground floor 6) Audience section 7) Supervisory and administrative rooms The purification system of this pool makes use of sandy filters and the required measures have been taken for installing ozonation systems and diatomite filters as complementary to the current filtering system. In order to expand the swimming pool in the future, there is the possibility to build an additional independent pool. In fact, parts of the mechanical equipment have been installed in the current powerhouse and refinery. The total cost of this project was 54 billion IRR at the time. Top

content: Ferdowsi University of Mashhad: Third University in Iran FUM Officials FUM Presidents A word from the President Vice Presidents Vice President for Academic Affairs College of Ferdowsi University of Mashhad Educational Planning and Academic Development Office E-Learning Center Vice President for Socio-Cultural and Student affairs Office of Cultural Affairs and Voluntary Activities Physical Education Administration Office of Health and Welfare Consulting Center for Cultural and Social Empowerment Vice President for Research and Technology Laboratory Network Management Office Office of Industrial Relations Research Management Office Center for Knowledge-based Business Incubator Unites in Humanities Director of FUM President’s Office and Public Relations The History Site Map Strategic Plan FUM Catalogs in Three Languages: English, French and Russian Center for Documents and Scientific Records of Eminent University Figures Information and Communication Technology (ICT) Center Campus Master Plan You are here: About / Campus Master Plan Ferdowsi University Campus Master Plan (FUCMP) Ferdowsi University Campus Master Plan (FUCMP) has been established in 2011 to set strong thinking about “Creating an environmentally sustainable campus and green development”. Studies on master plan programming, design, and implementation can be categorized into 14 chapters: 1. Basic Studies; 2. Educational Programming; 3. Spatial- Physical Cognition; 4. University’s Buildings Identification; 5. Principles of University Spaces Design; 6. World Case Study; 7. Spatial Analysis of Campus Land uses; 8. Physical Programming Principles; 9. Campus Design Principles; 10. Transportation and Traffic; 11. Campus Signs; 12. Landscape and Environment; 13. Passive Defense; 14. Building and Construction Details. In recent years, Islamic countries have considered “Islamic traditions and Contemporary Design” as the principles of university's outlook. Due to the physical needs and value-oriented viewpoints, the physical outlook of Ferdowsi University of Mashhad can be determined as below: Development and improvement of the university’s spatial needs following the sustainable development of Iranian- Islamic architecture patterns. Environment improvement, resource conservation, and green university achievement have been noted as the main goal of physical programming. Design strategies can be categorized into the UI GreenMeteric WUR criteria: 1. Setting and Infrastructures; 2. Energy and Climate Changes; 3. Waste; 4. Water; 5. Transportation and 6. Education. The ambition for achieving these criteria led the design team to focus on reducing environmental damages and spreading the use of renewable energies and green technologies. The main goals of FUM are as follows: Increasing place attachment and creating a strong sense of place; Developing a scientific, healthy, and creative environment; Creating sociable environments and desirable interaction; Considering architecture, urban and environmental design criteria (to achieve a green campus); Relationship between internal learning environments and external society; Promoting the current situation; Increasing environment legibility; Education, research, and experience in a responsive environment; Sustainable campus as an urban-regional sign. According to mentioned goals, the design strategies in the campus master plan are: Relationship with the city; Consideration of Iranian-Islamic architecture patterns following contemporary design principles; Green architecture design; Campus walkways development; Creating linking buildings; Space optimization; Environmentally adaptive architecture; Use of the latest space standards Considering future universities' architectural principles; Creating social learning centers in 9 zones of the campus; Creating a legible spatial network over the campus; Use of on-site ecological potentials and renovation of the stream as the ecologic axis; To legible the 12 faculties' borders; To unify the same land uses and avoid diffused buildings over the campus; To create recreational and desirable environments for students and other users; Green light transportation system on the main axis of the campus; The Legible entrances for campus; Creating a socio-physical area in heart of the campus; To increase accessibility to different destinations over the campus; Maximum use of current buildings and renovating them; Minimum of destruction and maximum flexibility in future buildings; Respect for the physical-spatial history of the campus and reviving the memories; and To achieve 90 sqm public per capita and 27 sqm spatial per capita for each student. Top

It includes the following units: medical, dental, environmental health, nursing, trusted doctors, drugstore, and ER. Medical Unit: This unit is responsible for the check-up and treatment of Ferdowsi University staff according to the schedule announced at the beginning of the new educational year. Dental Unit: Based on the schedule announced at the beginning of the new educational year, this unit offers services to the students and staff of Ferdowsi University who make prior appointments. These services are provided with a 45% discount for students and a 40% discount for the staff. Environmental Health Unit: The activities of this unit include inspection of the environmental health of cafeterias, dormitories, swimming pools, etc. This unit also offers educational materials and recruits active students and provides them with student jobs for the purpose of peer education. Nursing Unit: At this unit, all vaccinations recommended by the health center of the province, including tetanus, hepatitis, and rapidity are administrated, as well as drug injections, prescribed infusions, and all kinds of a wound dressing. Trusted Doctor: The examination and approval of medical certificates, medical exemptions, and the well-being of sports teams are this unit’s responsibility. Drugstore: This unit accepts prescriptions based on the pharmacopeia of the province’s health center. The working hours of this unit are from 13 to 14:30 and from 18 to 21. Ambulance: With one ambulance, this unit offers twenty-four seven services to patients and is ready to take them to medical centers across the city if necessary. Health Protection Plan: All undergraduate and graduate students receive medical check-up upon entering the university. They will be informed of the results via the student portal. Top

Studies on master plan programming, design, and implementation can be categorized into 14 chapters: 1. Basic Studies; 2. Educational Programming; 3. Spatial- Physical Cognition; 4. University’s Buildings Identification; 5. Principles of University Spaces Design; 6. World Case Study; 7. Spatial Analysis of Campus Land uses; 8. Physical Programming Principles; 9. Campus Design Principles; 10. Transportation and Traffic; 11. Campus Signs; 12. Landscape and Environment; 13. Passive Defense; 14. Building and Construction Details. In recent years, Islamic countries have considered “Islamic traditions and Contemporary Design” as the principles of university's outlook. Due to the physical needs and value-oriented viewpoints, the physical outlook of Ferdowsi University of Mashhad can be determined as below: Development and improvement of the university’s spatial needs following the sustainable development of Iranian- Islamic architecture patterns. Environment improvement, resource conservation, and green university achievement have been noted as the main goal of physical programming. Design strategies can be categorized into the UI GreenMeteric WUR criteria: 1. Setting and Infrastructures; 2. Energy and Climate Changes; 3. Waste; 4. Water; 5. Transportation and 6. Education. The ambition for achieving these criteria led the design team to focus on reducing environmental damages and spreading the use of renewable energies and green technologies. The main goals of FUM are as follows: Increasing place attachment and creating a strong sense of place; Developing a scientific, healthy, and creative environment; Creating sociable environments and desirable interaction; Considering architecture, urban and environmental design criteria (to achieve a green campus); Relationship between internal learning environments and external society; Promoting the current situation; Increasing environment legibility; Education, research, and experience in a responsive environment; Sustainable campus as an urban-regional sign. According to mentioned goals, the design strategies in the campus master plan are: Relationship with the city; Consideration of Iranian-Islamic architecture patterns following contemporary design principles; Green architecture design; Campus walkways development; Creating linking buildings; Space optimization; Environmentally adaptive architecture; Use of the latest space standards Considering future universities' architectural principles; Creating social learning centers in 9 zones of the campus; Creating a legible spatial network over the campus; Use of on-site ecological potentials and renovation of the stream as the ecologic axis; To legible the 12 faculties' borders; To unify the same land uses and avoid diffused buildings over the campus; To create recreational and desirable environments for students and other users; Green light transportation system on the main axis of the campus; The Legible entrances for campus; Creating a socio-physical area in heart of the campus; To increase accessibility to different destinations over the campus; Maximum use of current buildings and renovating them; Minimum of destruction and maximum flexibility in future buildings; Respect for the physical-spatial history of the campus and reviving the memories; and To achieve 90 sqm public per capita and 27 sqm spatial per capita for each student. content: Ferdowsi University of Mashhad: Third University in Iran The Information Center and Central Library (ICCL) Faculty Libraries Library of the Education and Psychology Library of Dr. Ali Shariati Letters and Humanities The Library of Morteza Motahhari Theology and Islamic Studies You are here: Libraries / Faculty Libraries / Library of Dr. Ali Shariati Faculty of Letters and Humanities Library of Dr. Ali Shariati Faculty of Letters and Humanities The library of Dr. Ali Shariati Faculty of Letters and Humanities was founded in 1956. The aim of this library is to identify, collect, organize, preserve and make the different types of library materials accessible. The library tries its best to support two important roles in the university namely research and education. The main mission of the library of Dr. Ali Shariati Faculty of Letters and Humanities is to support educational and research activities of all members of the university (i.e., students, teachers and staff). Currently, the library is stocked with approximately 75,000 volumes of books in Persian, 35,000 volumes in Latin languages (i.e., English and French) and 15,000 volumes in Arabic. This library holds several collections of donated books. These collections are donated by university professors namely Honorable Mahmood Farrokh, Dr. Ali Akbar Fayyaz, Siavash Parvaz, Dr. Mahmood Ramyar, Hassan Lahooti and Mohammad Ghahraman. A valuable collection of written cultural heritage is also preserved in the library. In the Manuscripts Section of the library there are 521 manuscripts, including Mahmood Farrokh, Ali Akbar Fayyaz and others distinguished persons’ collections. Over 800 exquisite and lithography volumes are also kept in this collection. The library is located in an area of over 1400 square meters in two floors with a team of 6 professional staff who provide services in two time shifts. Library Services Lending and renewal of books Providing scans from manuscripts and reference sources for users at the national and international levels Providing services to students and researchers from other universities Library instructions including workshops and library tours for new undergraduate and post-graduate students Providing information literacy workshops regarding instructions on the use of databases and software in related fields of studies. Needless to say that the social and cultural characteristics of the university, as well as scientific and research activities are in line with the grand plans of the Islamic Republic of Iran in achieving both spiritual and physical development. Therefore, the Vice-President for Socio-Cultural Affairs of the Ferdowsi University of Mashhad tries to prepare the required frameworks and preparations for social and cultural development of all university members (students, faculty and staff) with the help of its experienced and knowledgeable academics. In this regard, the university students who are the largest group of academic members of the university and the future generation of Iran, have always had the most prominent role in the cultural and social programs of the university and they have had great achievements in these affairs. In recent years, the Ferdowsi University of Mashhad has always been a leading model in terms of being a cultural and academic community. Although the Vice-President for Socio-Cultural Affairs has followed wonderful strategies to train skilled experts in social and cultural aspects of academic life, it is still behind its ideal status. Major Goals Encouraging community participation, social discipline, and improvement of mental and social health and vitality Expanding and deepening constructive interactions and synergy with scientific, cultural, social, sports and economic centers at national and international levels Enhancing students and graduates’ sense of commitment to the university Developing and upgrading the infrastructure and cultural, physical, and technological areas in the university. Activities The activities of this office can be divided into three general categories: Supervision, support and organization of university students’ associations: To supervise, support and organize students’ associations such as art and culture centers, science foundations (there are more than ninety specialized foundations and twenty interdisciplinary centers at FUM), Basij and Islamic associations (the Islamic University Students’ Association, Islamic Society of Students, and Islamic Association of Neo-thinker Students) and publications (more than 80 students publications) Supervision, support and organization of staff and professors’ associations Additional activities are related to pilgrimage center, movies center, recreational services, campus galleries, audio-visual center, reunion, and camps centers. Since 2007 the mission of the college is divided into two parts : Main mission: Managing, planning and holding a higher education open system . Sub-mission: Conducting a variety of training services needed by the society . The College pursues the following goals To improve the level of education and culture To create appropriate basis for increasing access to higher education To expand and develop professional and practical environment in the higher education system To reduce the social demand for official education in higher education institutions To provide ongoing training courses for graduates of universities and higher education institutions. Types of Training A. Open Higher Education The mission of Open Higher Education covers curriculum planning and implementation of courses that are required for different sectors of the society, such as organizations, public and private institutions, and industries. Regardless of the existing obstacles such as the entrance exam, the Open Higher Education System facilitates everyone’s access to the acquisition of academic knowledge. In such an educational system, syllabi are designed according to the needs of the learners. B. Minor Courses Minor courses are the ones which talented students of the second year onwards in the Bachelor’s program can participate in under special conditions such as having good GPA score. Passing 21 to 25 units of specialized courses in another Bachelor’s majors offered at Ferdowsi University of Mashhad through these courses, students will become familiar with other majors and specialties that are of their interest. C. Training and entrepreneurial courses The training and entrepreneurial courses are the ones in which students of a particular major will be well acquainted with the practical issues of their profession that are not covered in the framework of the Bachelor’s program. These courses are concerned with practical issues, workshops, and executive projects. Training and entrepreneurial courses can also be up to about 24 units. All Ferdowsi University students (undergraduate and postgraduate) can participate in the training and entrepreneurial courses supervised by the College of Ferdowsi University of Mashhad and are held by different departments. Training and entrepreneurial courses are between 21 and 24 units. Training courses consist of theoretical discussions and practical activities as well as workshops, fieldwork's, projects and similar other courses. Entrepreneurial courses comprise elective courses. Students of other universities and educational institutions can also enroll in these courses. However, students of Ferdowsi University of Mashhad are in priority. Virtual universities have changed the concept of traditional classes. Although the activities, which are held in virtual classes are similar to those in traditional classes, the environment is totally different. Ferdowsi University of Mashhad has been one of the pioneers in e-learning. The idea of having virtual classes was put forward in 2001 at Ferdowsi University of Mashhad. The virtual university committee, under the supervision of Information, and Communication Center was formed afterward. This committee aims at developing the basic requirements for establishing a virtual university and its administrative aspects. The result of a research project led to the authorization issued by the Ferdowsi University of Mashhad Board of Directors and the Ministry of Science, Research and Technology to establish one virtual major in the Bachelor’s and nine virtual majors in the Master’s program. This led to the establishment of E-learning Center at Ferdowsi university of Mashhad in 2001. It was established to put more emphasis on e-learning and to develop the idea of electronic education. At the moment, more than 35 undergraduate virtual university subjects are offered in every semester. Summer semester classes are also offered virtually at Ferdowsi University of Mashhad. In addition, the content of more than 100 subjects of Bachelor’s programs is available virtually on e-learning portals. They can either be used as e-learning materials or supplemental online materials to traditional classes. Aims To embed Communication and Information Technology in educational programs to promote the quality of education at Ferdowsi University of Mashhad To enhance the quality of course contents by modern strategies and technologies To help education move beyond time and place limitations To benefit from the knowledge of national and internal professors To offer audience knowledge and skills in a relaxed atmosphere while they are at work or in their family life Activities Offering university courses and majors electronically Offering individual subjects electronically inside and outside the university Preparing course contents based on the SCORM standard Video-recording of class presentations of all faculties to upload to the online e-learning center portal Organizing and supporting conferences, meetings, and seminars electronically Holding and supporting on-line thesis defense sessions in all faculties Collaborating with other universities and institutions to hold virtual supplementary classes Supporting on-line interview and introductory sessions Equipping faculties with facilities available in the e-learning center Holding workshops for faculty members to help them embed information technology in their teaching and enhance educational programs. title: Commencement of the master plan for developing technologies to improve subsurface imaging in the exploration of hydrocarbon resources in the Kopeh Dagh sedimentary basin at Ferdowsi University of Mash :: Ferdowsi University of Mashhad :: Ferdowsi University of Mashhad: Third University in Iran
content: Commencement of the master plan for developing technologies to improve subsurface imaging in the exploration of hydrocarbon resources in the Kopeh Dagh sedimentary basin at Ferdowsi University of Mash :: Ferdowsi University of Mashhad :: Ferdowsi University of Mashhad: Third University in Iran The first phase of the master plan "Development of subsurface imaging improvement technologies in hydrocarbon resource exploration in the Kopeh Dagh sedimentary basin" to create technological capabilities in the oil and gas exploration sector and form an innovation network and business formation in the field of subsurface imaging technologies, has been defined as follows and successfully implemented under difficult sanctions conditions. The technology development roadmap has been developed within the framework of the first package, and accordingly, the research projects of the second package have been defined in two phases and under the title of completing the database data by providing a program to conduct the necessary studies and experiments at three laboratory, semi-industrial and industrial scales. Currently, the first phase of the second package, including 6 projects, has been completed with 100% realization of the anticipated goals. In addition to the universities of Tehran (Institute of Geophysics and Institute of Petroleum), Amirkabir University of Technology, Zanjan Postgraduate Education, and Daqing Normal University, international companies and experts from Russia, Switzerland, Norway, and Mexico have participated in the research project with Ferdowsi University of Mashhad. In the continuation of the implementation of the second phase of the second package of the plan, five project titles with a credit of over 190 billion rials and 2 million and 800 thousand euros have been approved and announced. Considering the university's scientific, administrative capacities, and valuable infrastructure in the fields of reservoir exploration studies, geomechanical studies, and increased recovery, as well as the network of partners formed during the implementation of the plan, Ferdowsi University of Mashhad has announced its readiness to launch a Center for New Exploration Technologies.

title: Joint meeting of the President of Ferdowsi University of Mashhad with Rear Admiral Habibollah Sayyari :: Ferdowsi University of Mashhad :: Ferdowsi University of Mashhad: Third University in Iran
content: Joint meeting of the President of Ferdowsi University of Mashhad with Rear Admiral Habibollah Sayyari :: Ferdowsi University of Mashhad :: Ferdowsi University of Mashhad: Third University in Iran Prof. Javan Jafari, the President of Ferdowsi University of Mashhad, met and discussed with Rear Admiral Habibollah Sayyari, Deputy Coordinator of the General Command of the Islamic Republic of Iran Army on Sunday, June 25, 2025, In this meeting, which was attended by a group of commanders of the Navy, Air Force, Passive Defense, and Rangers of the Islamic Republic of Iran Army, in addition to emphasizing the expansion of cooperation between Ferdowsi University of Mashhad and the executive branches, issues such as utilizing the capacity and capabilities of Ferdowsi University of Mashhad students and the capacities of the Faculty of Engineering in the field of defense production were discussed. Admiral Sayyari, while expressing his pleasure at being at Ferdowsi University of Mashhad and the invitation to participate in the grand program linking epics from Toos to Khorramshahr, considered such programs to be a factor in strengthening religious and national identity. In this regard, he appreciated and thanked the university president.

Studies on master plan programming, design, and implementation can be categorized into 14 chapters: 1. Basic Studies; 2. Educational Programming; 3. Spatial- Physical Cognition; 4. University’s Buildings Identification; 5. Principles of University Spaces Design; 6. World Case Study; 7. Spatial Analysis of Campus Land uses; 8. Physical Programming Principles; 9. Campus Design Principles; 10. Transportation and Traffic; 11. Campus Signs; 12. Landscape and Environment; 13. Passive Defense; 14. Building and Construction Details. In recent years, Islamic countries have considered “Islamic traditions and Contemporary Design” as the principles of university's outlook. Due to the physical needs and value-oriented viewpoints, the physical outlook of Ferdowsi University of Mashhad can be determined as below: Development and improvement of the university’s spatial needs following the sustainable development of Iranian- Islamic architecture patterns. Environment improvement, resource conservation, and green university achievement have been noted as the main goal of physical programming. Design strategies can be categorized into the UI GreenMeteric WUR criteria: 1. Setting and Infrastructures; 2. Energy and Climate Changes; 3. Waste; 4. Water; 5. Transportation and 6. Education. The ambition for achieving these criteria led the design team to focus on reducing environmental damages and spreading the use of renewable energies and green technologies. The main goals of FUM are as follows: Increasing place attachment and creating a strong sense of place; Developing a scientific, healthy, and creative environment; Creating sociable environments and desirable interaction; Considering architecture, urban and environmental design criteria (to achieve a green campus); Relationship between internal learning environments and external society; Promoting the current situation; Increasing environment legibility; Education, research, and experience in a responsive environment; Sustainable campus as an urban-regional sign. According to mentioned goals, the design strategies in the campus master plan are: Relationship with the city; Consideration of Iranian-Islamic architecture patterns following contemporary design principles; Green architecture design; Campus walkways development; Creating linking buildings; Space optimization; Environmentally adaptive architecture; Use of the latest space standards Considering future universities' architectural principles; Creating social learning centers in 9 zones of the campus; Creating a legible spatial network over the campus; Use of on-site ecological potentials and renovation of the stream as the ecologic axis; To legible the 12 faculties' borders; To unify the same land uses and avoid diffused buildings over the campus; To create recreational and desirable environments for students and other users; Green light transportation system on the main axis of the campus; The Legible entrances for campus; Creating a socio-physical area in heart of the campus; To increase accessibility to different destinations over the campus; Maximum use of current buildings and renovating them; Minimum of destruction and maximum flexibility in future buildings; Respect for the physical-spatial history of the campus and reviving the memories; and To achieve 90 sqm public per capita and 27 sqm spatial per capita for each student. title: Publication of a new book by a faculty member of Ferdowsi University of Mashhad by Elsevier International Publishing
content: Publication of a new book by a faculty member of Ferdowsi University of Mashhad by Elsevier International Publishing Dr. Parisa Taheri, a faculty member of the Department of Plant Protection, Faculty of Agriculture, Ferdowsi University of Mashhad, published her new book titled “Environmentally Safe Strategies for Plant Protection Against Biotic and Abiotic Stresses” in the prestigious international publication Elsevier. This book examines and analyzes safe and environmentally friendly mechanisms and methods for protecting plants against biotic and abiotic stresses. Given the increasing global demand for organic food and animal feed, the study and application of natural and biological compounds to promote plant growth and protect agricultural products has become increasingly important. In this work, the role of natural compounds extracted from plants, fungi, and beneficial microorganisms, as well as their metabolites, in strengthening plant defense systems and mitigating environmental stresses has been comprehensively investigated. These compounds can be used as biological control agents with direct or indirect effects within the framework of sustainable and organic agriculture. The aforementioned book, comprising 15 chapters and written in collaboration with prominent researchers from four continents and 12 countries, is a valuable resource for researchers, students, and specialists in the fields of plant medicine, agricultural biotechnology, plant biology, plant physiology, plant microbiology, and environmental sciences.

title: Publication of an article by a faculty member of Ferdowsi University of Mashhad in the prestigious journal Science
content: Publication of an article by a faculty member of Ferdowsi University of Mashhad in the prestigious journal Science Dr. Mansour Aliabadian, a faculty member of the Department of Biology at the Faculty of Science, Ferdowsi University of Mashhad, in collaboration with 44 international researchers, has successfully published an article in the prestigious journal Science. This study examined color variation in four species of light-winged songbirds from the genus wheatears, birds known for their distinctive black and white patterns on the body, throat, and neck feathers. The results of the study show that although the ASIP locus is the primary factor in black pigmentation, each part of the body is affected by different regulatory factors, leading to the emergence of significant color variation. In addition, extensive genetic crossing between different species has caused the transfer of the old white haplotype from the eastern black-eared wheatear (Oenanthe melanoleuca) and the emergence of new mutations with similar patterns in other species. These findings demonstrate that even traits controlled by a single gene can be influenced by complex networks of regulatory factors, thereby playing a crucial role in the processes of evolution and biodiversity. Link to access the article on the Science magazine website: https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.ado8005

Although technological changes have brought different types of activities to the center since the past four decades, this center is now more focused on the development and use of ICT in different sectors of the university including educational, research, administrative and executive sections. The Ferdowsi University of Mashhad is one of the few universities where the efficient management of its ICT center has led to the creation of integrated websites and computer networks. These websites and computer networks offer a wide range of services to the students, staff, and faculty members. These services have also been offered to more than 50 universities and institutes of higher education in the form of SADAF (Information Systems of the Ferdowsi University of Mashhad). The Information and Communication Technology (ICT) Center has so far achieved outstanding ranks at the national level leading to the winning of many awards and certificates. content: Ferdowsi University of Mashhad: Third University in Iran FUM Officials FUM Presidents A word from the President Vice Presidents Vice President for Academic Affairs College of Ferdowsi University of Mashhad Educational Planning and Academic Development Office E-Learning Center Vice President for Socio-Cultural and Student affairs Office of Cultural Affairs and Voluntary Activities Physical Education Administration Office of Health and Welfare Consulting Center for Cultural and Social Empowerment Vice President for Research and Technology Laboratory Network Management Office Office of Industrial Relations Research Management Office Center for Knowledge-based Business Incubator Unites in Humanities Director of FUM President’s Office and Public Relations The History Site Map Strategic Plan FUM Catalogs in Three Languages: English, French and Russian Center for Documents and Scientific Records of Eminent University Figures Information and Communication Technology (ICT) Center Campus Master Plan You are here: About / Campus Master Plan Ferdowsi University Campus Master Plan (FUCMP) Ferdowsi University Campus Master Plan (FUCMP) has been established in 2011 to set strong thinking about “Creating an environmentally sustainable campus and green development”. Studies on master plan programming, design, and implementation can be categorized into 14 chapters: 1. Basic Studies; 2. Educational Programming; 3. Spatial- Physical Cognition; 4. University’s Buildings Identification; 5. Principles of University Spaces Design; 6. World Case Study; 7. Spatial Analysis of Campus Land uses; 8. Physical Programming Principles; 9. Campus Design Principles; 10. Transportation and Traffic; 11. Campus Signs; 12. Landscape and Environment; 13. Passive Defense; 14. Building and Construction Details. In recent years, Islamic countries have considered “Islamic traditions and Contemporary Design” as the principles of university's outlook. Due to the physical needs and value-oriented viewpoints, the physical outlook of Ferdowsi University of Mashhad can be determined as below: Development and improvement of the university’s spatial needs following the sustainable development of Iranian- Islamic architecture patterns. Environment improvement, resource conservation, and green university achievement have been noted as the main goal of physical programming. Design strategies can be categorized into the UI GreenMeteric WUR criteria: 1. Setting and Infrastructures; 2. Energy and Climate Changes; 3. Waste; 4. Water; 5. Transportation and 6. Education. The ambition for achieving these criteria led the design team to focus on reducing environmental damages and spreading the use of renewable energies and green technologies. The main goals of FUM are as follows: Increasing place attachment and creating a strong sense of place; Developing a scientific, healthy, and creative environment; Creating sociable environments and desirable interaction; Considering architecture, urban and environmental design criteria (to achieve a green campus); Relationship between internal learning environments and external society; Promoting the current situation; Increasing environment legibility; Education, research, and experience in a responsive environment; Sustainable campus as an urban-regional sign. According to mentioned goals, the design strategies in the campus master plan are: Relationship with the city; Consideration of Iranian-Islamic architecture patterns following contemporary design principles; Green architecture design; Campus walkways development; Creating linking buildings; Space optimization; Environmentally adaptive architecture; Use of the latest space standards Considering future universities' architectural principles; Creating social learning centers in 9 zones of the campus; Creating a legible spatial network over the campus; Use of on-site ecological potentials and renovation of the stream as the ecologic axis; To legible the 12 faculties' borders; To unify the same land uses and avoid diffused buildings over the campus; To create recreational and desirable environments for students and other users; Green light transportation system on the main axis of the campus; The Legible entrances for campus; Creating a socio-physical area in heart of the campus; To increase accessibility to different destinations over the campus; Maximum use of current buildings and renovating them; Minimum of destruction and maximum flexibility in future buildings; Respect for the physical-spatial history of the campus and reviving the memories; and To achieve 90 sqm public per capita and 27 sqm spatial per capita for each student. This office is responsible for organizing, coordinating and monitoring the performance of the University schools and departments. In addition, the Vice-President for Education is responsible for the following duties: To evaluate and monitor the academic performance of faculty members and academic administrators To design and implement programs for the promotion of faculty members To revise and modify the curriculum To plan for the development of different academic programs and new fields of study To identify, cluster and support talented students To design academic courses, produce content, and implement electronic instruction programs To establish and manage the Free and Virtual Training Center . However, the first step was converting the Higher Institute of Public Health to a Medical Faculty in 1949. Shortly after, the Medical Faculty admitted its first group of medical students, and in December 1949 this institute was officially inaugurated as the first Center for Medical Sciences in the North East of Iran by the Minister of Culture, the late Dr. Zanganeh. Finally in 1956 after the foundation of the facultys of Literature and Theology, the complex was named "Mashhad University". Later on in 1957, the rules and regulations for employment and education of Tehran University were adopted for use in this new university. Since then other faculties have been gradually added to the university based on the local demand. These are the Faculty of Science (1961), the Faculty of Education, the Faculty of Agriculture (1973), the Faculty of Engineering (1975), the Faculty of Economics and Administrative Sciences (1987), the Faculty of Veterinary Medicine (1991), the Faculty of Mathematics (1996), the Faculty of Architecture, the Faculty of Urbanism and Islamic Arts, and the Faculty of Natural Resources and Environment (2001). In 1975 after the separation of the facultys related to the Medical Sciences from the university, the name of the university was changed from "Mashhad University” to "The Ferdowsi University of Mashhad". The Ferdowsi University of Mashhad has now nearly seven decades of brilliant educational, research and cultural history and it is well known among institutes of higher education in Iran. It is currently one of the nation’s top three universities and also the largest center of higher education in the North East of Iran. At present, the Ferdowsi University of Mashhad is composed of 12 facultys , 38 research centers, 7 centers of excellence, 820 faculty members (%50 of whom are professors or associate professors), over 20000 students (9996 undergraduate, 6143 Masters, and 3905 Ph.D. students), and 1050 staff members. Currently, 1279 foreign students are enrolled in different academic programs at the Ferdowsi University of Mashhad. In addition, there are also 187 foreign students who are passing their six-month training courses in language at the International Center for Teaching Persian to Non-Persian Speakers. These students would begin their academic education after they pass this six-month course of study. The transfer time is usually quite short. Otherwise, International flights to Tehran (IKA airport) are more common and there are direct flights from many countries. Mashhad is about 900 km far from Tehran and is accessible via flights, trains, and buses. For taking flights you must switch to THR (Mehrabad) airport. IKA and THR airports are connected by airport taxicabs which service 24/7 (around 18 €; reservation NOT needed). Round trip ticket to Mashhad costs approximately 100 € with the flight time of 1h15. Train tickets are half cheaper but they are usually packed and need to be booked well in advance. Traveling time via railways is about 10 hours. The IKA airport is connected to the train station by airport taxicabs (costs around 20 €; reservation NOT needed). Traveling by public bus is the cheapest but unexpected events may happen (delay, canceling, etc.). Car rental is not that common in Iran; it is expensive and the process is quite complicated. In case you arrive in Tehran, we will arrange to send someone to the airport to help you with airport transfer. When you get to Mashhad, our welcoming committee will pick you up from the airport and accompany you to Ferdowsi University of Mashhad. The same will be arranged for your departure. N.B. local tickets (Tehran-Mashhad-Tehran) cannot be booked via International credit/debit cards and the reservation should be made via national bank cards. Please communicate with us (intr@um.ac.ir) your dates of arrival and departure and we will book your local tickets with the lowest price possible. Please do not hesitate to contact us if you have any further questions or concerns: Email: intr@um.ac.ir Phone:  +985138802415 Fax: +985138836056 Postal Code: 9177948974 Top

Studies on master plan programming, design, and implementation can be categorized into 14 chapters: 1. Basic Studies; 2. Educational Programming; 3. Spatial- Physical Cognition; 4. University’s Buildings Identification; 5. Principles of University Spaces Design; 6. World Case Study; 7. Spatial Analysis of Campus Land uses; 8. Physical Programming Principles; 9. Campus Design Principles; 10. Transportation and Traffic; 11. Campus Signs; 12. Landscape and Environment; 13. Passive Defense; 14. Building and Construction Details. In recent years, Islamic countries have considered “Islamic traditions and Contemporary Design” as the principles of university's outlook. Due to the physical needs and value-oriented viewpoints, the physical outlook of Ferdowsi University of Mashhad can be determined as below: Development and improvement of the university’s spatial needs following the sustainable development of Iranian- Islamic architecture patterns. Environment improvement, resource conservation, and green university achievement have been noted as the main goal of physical programming. Design strategies can be categorized into the UI GreenMeteric WUR criteria: 1. Setting and Infrastructures; 2. Energy and Climate Changes; 3. Waste; 4. Water; 5. Transportation and 6. Education. The ambition for achieving these criteria led the design team to focus on reducing environmental damages and spreading the use of renewable energies and green technologies. The main goals of FUM are as follows: Increasing place attachment and creating a strong sense of place; Developing a scientific, healthy, and creative environment; Creating sociable environments and desirable interaction; Considering architecture, urban and environmental design criteria (to achieve a green campus); Relationship between internal learning environments and external society; Promoting the current situation; Increasing environment legibility; Education, research, and experience in a responsive environment; Sustainable campus as an urban-regional sign. According to mentioned goals, the design strategies in the campus master plan are: Relationship with the city; Consideration of Iranian-Islamic architecture patterns following contemporary design principles; Green architecture design; Campus walkways development; Creating linking buildings; Space optimization; Environmentally adaptive architecture; Use of the latest space standards Considering future universities' architectural principles; Creating social learning centers in 9 zones of the campus; Creating a legible spatial network over the campus; Use of on-site ecological potentials and renovation of the stream as the ecologic axis; To legible the 12 faculties' borders; To unify the same land uses and avoid diffused buildings over the campus; To create recreational and desirable environments for students and other users; Green light transportation system on the main axis of the campus; The Legible entrances for campus; Creating a socio-physical area in heart of the campus; To increase accessibility to different destinations over the campus; Maximum use of current buildings and renovating them; Minimum of destruction and maximum flexibility in future buildings; Respect for the physical-spatial history of the campus and reviving the memories; and To achieve 90 sqm public per capita and 27 sqm spatial per capita for each student. Enrollment at the university 2. Referring to the consular affairs center, presenting university’s admission letter and identity documents, filling out the relevant forms and providing the 1st page of the passport 3. Presenting the passport which is valid for a minimum of 8 months and applying for study visa 4. Receiving a number for student visa, referring to the Iranian embassy at your city, receiving student visa and referring to the consular affairs department 5. Applying for the issuance of residency 6. Presenting birth certificate and/or local affidavit, Parents’ identity documents, and passport pages. Receiving a registration permission letter from the consular affairs department and presenting it to the university *Female students can only apply for their children and residency would not be issued for their husband and/or other members of their family. Therefore, it is obligatory to present the letter designating that the husband has transferred the custody of the child/children to the female student. This letter has to be approved by the Iranian Ministry of Foreign Affairs. *Male students can apply for the residency of their wife and children, but residency would not be issued for other members of their family. Accordingly, it is obligatory to present the marriage certificate approved by the Iranian Ministry of Foreign Affairs. Also, if the children have been born in Iran, a birth certificate confirming this claim must be presented. Top

Several regional and national authorities participated at this inauguration ceremony. As the first speaker, Dr Alireza Ashuri, the President of Ferdowsi University of Mashhad at the time, said: This pool has been constructed based on updated international standards in order to provide students, employees and faculty members with high-quality sport amenities. Features of the Covered Swimming pool at FUM With a total area of 6350 square meters, the covered swimming pool of Ferdowsi University of Mashhad is considered as one of the biggest pools in Iranian universities and the only standard swimming pool for professional competitions in Khorasan Razavi Province. The complex includes the following facilities: 1) Main pool (50*25 m) for standard professional competitions 2) Children’s pool (6*8 m) 3) Steam sauna, dry sauna, Jacuzzi 4) Hydrotherapy section, fitness room 5) Uncovered cafeteria on the 1st floor and coffee shop on the ground floor 6) Audience section 7) Supervisory and administrative rooms The purification system of this pool makes use of sandy filters and the required measures have been taken for installing ozonation systems and diatomite filters as complementary to the current filtering system. In order to expand the swimming pool in the future, there is the possibility to build an additional independent pool. In fact, parts of the mechanical equipment have been installed in the current powerhouse and refinery. The total cost of this project was 54 billion IRR at the time. Top
