content: Ferdowsi University of Mashhad: Third University in Iran FUM Officials FUM Presidents A word from the President Vice Presidents Vice President for Academic Affairs College of Ferdowsi University of Mashhad Educational Planning and Academic Development Office E-Learning Center Vice President for Socio-Cultural and Student affairs Office of Cultural Affairs and Voluntary Activities Physical Education Administration Office of Health and Welfare Consulting Center for Cultural and Social Empowerment Vice President for Research and Technology Laboratory Network Management Office Office of Industrial Relations Research Management Office Center for Knowledge-based Business Incubator Unites in Humanities Director of FUM President’s Office and Public Relations The History Site Map Strategic Plan FUM Catalogs in Three Languages: English, French and Russian Center for Documents and Scientific Records of Eminent University Figures Information and Communication Technology (ICT) Center Campus Master Plan You are here: About / Campus Master Plan Ferdowsi University Campus Master Plan (FUCMP) Ferdowsi University Campus Master Plan (FUCMP) has been established in 2011 to set strong thinking about “Creating an environmentally sustainable campus and green development”. Studies on master plan programming, design, and implementation can be categorized into 14 chapters: 1. Basic Studies; 2. Educational Programming; 3. Spatial- Physical Cognition; 4. University’s Buildings Identification; 5. Principles of University Spaces Design; 6. World Case Study; 7. Spatial Analysis of Campus Land uses; 8. Physical Programming Principles; 9. Campus Design Principles; 10. Transportation and Traffic; 11. Campus Signs; 12. Landscape and Environment; 13. Passive Defense; 14. Building and Construction Details. In recent years, Islamic countries have considered “Islamic traditions and Contemporary Design” as the principles of university's outlook. Due to the physical needs and value-oriented viewpoints, the physical outlook of Ferdowsi University of Mashhad can be determined as below: Development and improvement of the university’s spatial needs following the sustainable development of Iranian- Islamic architecture patterns. Environment improvement, resource conservation, and green university achievement have been noted as the main goal of physical programming. Design strategies can be categorized into the UI GreenMeteric WUR criteria: 1. Setting and Infrastructures; 2. Energy and Climate Changes; 3. Waste; 4. Water; 5. Transportation and 6. Education. The ambition for achieving these criteria led the design team to focus on reducing environmental damages and spreading the use of renewable energies and green technologies. The main goals of FUM are as follows: Increasing place attachment and creating a strong sense of place; Developing a scientific, healthy, and creative environment; Creating sociable environments and desirable interaction; Considering architecture, urban and environmental design criteria (to achieve a green campus); Relationship between internal learning environments and external society; Promoting the current situation; Increasing environment legibility; Education, research, and experience in a responsive environment; Sustainable campus as an urban-regional sign. According to mentioned goals, the design strategies in the campus master plan are: Relationship with the city; Consideration of Iranian-Islamic architecture patterns following contemporary design principles; Green architecture design; Campus walkways development; Creating linking buildings; Space optimization; Environmentally adaptive architecture; Use of the latest space standards Considering future universities' architectural principles; Creating social learning centers in 9 zones of the campus; Creating a legible spatial network over the campus; Use of on-site ecological potentials and renovation of the stream as the ecologic axis; To legible the 12 faculties' borders; To unify the same land uses and avoid diffused buildings over the campus; To create recreational and desirable environments for students and other users; Green light transportation system on the main axis of the campus; The Legible entrances for campus; Creating a socio-physical area in heart of the campus; To increase accessibility to different destinations over the campus; Maximum use of current buildings and renovating them; Minimum of destruction and maximum flexibility in future buildings; Respect for the physical-spatial history of the campus and reviving the memories; and To achieve 90 sqm public per capita and 27 sqm spatial per capita for each student. It includes the following units: medical, dental, environmental health, nursing, trusted doctors, drugstore, and ER. Medical Unit: This unit is responsible for the check-up and treatment of Ferdowsi University staff according to the schedule announced at the beginning of the new educational year. Dental Unit: Based on the schedule announced at the beginning of the new educational year, this unit offers services to the students and staff of Ferdowsi University who make prior appointments. These services are provided with a 45% discount for students and a 40% discount for the staff. Environmental Health Unit: The activities of this unit include inspection of the environmental health of cafeterias, dormitories, swimming pools, etc. This unit also offers educational materials and recruits active students and provides them with student jobs for the purpose of peer education. Nursing Unit: At this unit, all vaccinations recommended by the health center of the province, including tetanus, hepatitis, and rapidity are administrated, as well as drug injections, prescribed infusions, and all kinds of a wound dressing. Trusted Doctor: The examination and approval of medical certificates, medical exemptions, and the well-being of sports teams are this unit’s responsibility. Drugstore: This unit accepts prescriptions based on the pharmacopeia of the province’s health center. The working hours of this unit are from 13 to 14:30 and from 18 to 21. Ambulance: With one ambulance, this unit offers twenty-four seven services to patients and is ready to take them to medical centers across the city if necessary. Health Protection Plan: All undergraduate and graduate students receive medical check-up upon entering the university. They will be informed of the results via the student portal. Top

It has affiliations with its counterparts around the globe. It is the primary agency for the implementation of the university’s international strategy, and acts as a point of contact between FUM and the international academic community. Office of International Students The Ferdowsi University of Mashhad is considered one of the top universities in Iran and in the region. FUM is a comprehensive university covering all branches of sciences including Humanities, Pure Sciences, Technology, Agriculture and Architecture. Students from other countries can apply and continue their studies in this qualified university . The Ferdowsi University of Mashhad, as a green university, benefits from a beautiful campus, excellent facilities and friendly environment in which all international students feel at home. These facilities include: standard and well-equipped dormitories, restaurants, rich libraries, vast IT and transportation services, good medical services, counseling services, numerous shops, sports and recreational complexes, etc . Studies on master plan programming, design, and implementation can be categorized into 14 chapters: 1. Basic Studies; 2. Educational Programming; 3. Spatial- Physical Cognition; 4. University’s Buildings Identification; 5. Principles of University Spaces Design; 6. World Case Study; 7. Spatial Analysis of Campus Land uses; 8. Physical Programming Principles; 9. Campus Design Principles; 10. Transportation and Traffic; 11. Campus Signs; 12. Landscape and Environment; 13. Passive Defense; 14. Building and Construction Details. In recent years, Islamic countries have considered “Islamic traditions and Contemporary Design” as the principles of university's outlook. Due to the physical needs and value-oriented viewpoints, the physical outlook of Ferdowsi University of Mashhad can be determined as below: Development and improvement of the university’s spatial needs following the sustainable development of Iranian- Islamic architecture patterns. Environment improvement, resource conservation, and green university achievement have been noted as the main goal of physical programming. Design strategies can be categorized into the UI GreenMeteric WUR criteria: 1. Setting and Infrastructures; 2. Energy and Climate Changes; 3. Waste; 4. Water; 5. Transportation and 6. Education. The ambition for achieving these criteria led the design team to focus on reducing environmental damages and spreading the use of renewable energies and green technologies. The main goals of FUM are as follows: Increasing place attachment and creating a strong sense of place; Developing a scientific, healthy, and creative environment; Creating sociable environments and desirable interaction; Considering architecture, urban and environmental design criteria (to achieve a green campus); Relationship between internal learning environments and external society; Promoting the current situation; Increasing environment legibility; Education, research, and experience in a responsive environment; Sustainable campus as an urban-regional sign. According to mentioned goals, the design strategies in the campus master plan are: Relationship with the city; Consideration of Iranian-Islamic architecture patterns following contemporary design principles; Green architecture design; Campus walkways development; Creating linking buildings; Space optimization; Environmentally adaptive architecture; Use of the latest space standards Considering future universities' architectural principles; Creating social learning centers in 9 zones of the campus; Creating a legible spatial network over the campus; Use of on-site ecological potentials and renovation of the stream as the ecologic axis; To legible the 12 faculties' borders; To unify the same land uses and avoid diffused buildings over the campus; To create recreational and desirable environments for students and other users; Green light transportation system on the main axis of the campus; The Legible entrances for campus; Creating a socio-physical area in heart of the campus; To increase accessibility to different destinations over the campus; Maximum use of current buildings and renovating them; Minimum of destruction and maximum flexibility in future buildings; Respect for the physical-spatial history of the campus and reviving the memories; and To achieve 90 sqm public per capita and 27 sqm spatial per capita for each student. content: Ferdowsi University of Mashhad: Third University in Iran The Information Center and Central Library (ICCL) Faculty Libraries Library of the Education and Psychology Library of Dr. Ali Shariati Letters and Humanities The Library of Morteza Motahhari Theology and Islamic Studies You are here: Libraries / Faculty Libraries / Library of Dr. Ali Shariati Faculty of Letters and Humanities Library of Dr. Ali Shariati Faculty of Letters and Humanities The library of Dr. Ali Shariati Faculty of Letters and Humanities was founded in 1956. The aim of this library is to identify, collect, organize, preserve and make the different types of library materials accessible. The library tries its best to support two important roles in the university namely research and education. The main mission of the library of Dr. Ali Shariati Faculty of Letters and Humanities is to support educational and research activities of all members of the university (i.e., students, teachers and staff). Currently, the library is stocked with approximately 75,000 volumes of books in Persian, 35,000 volumes in Latin languages (i.e., English and French) and 15,000 volumes in Arabic. This library holds several collections of donated books. These collections are donated by university professors namely Honorable Mahmood Farrokh, Dr. Ali Akbar Fayyaz, Siavash Parvaz, Dr. Mahmood Ramyar, Hassan Lahooti and Mohammad Ghahraman. A valuable collection of written cultural heritage is also preserved in the library. In the Manuscripts Section of the library there are 521 manuscripts, including Mahmood Farrokh, Ali Akbar Fayyaz and others distinguished persons’ collections. Over 800 exquisite and lithography volumes are also kept in this collection. The library is located in an area of over 1400 square meters in two floors with a team of 6 professional staff who provide services in two time shifts. Library Services Lending and renewal of books Providing scans from manuscripts and reference sources for users at the national and international levels Providing services to students and researchers from other universities Library instructions including workshops and library tours for new undergraduate and post-graduate students Providing information literacy workshops regarding instructions on the use of databases and software in related fields of studies. Currently, we have representative members from a variety of fields such as Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Civil Engineering, Applied Mathematics, and Biological Sciences. At the Center of Excellence for Soft Computing and Intelligent Information Processing, our basic belief is that intelligent systems and knowledge engineering can and will play a fundamental role in the betterment of human lives. We are committed to advance the state of the art in these paradigms, to address the open and difficult problems of humanity, to build closer ties with various related industries, and to train well-qualified experts. Being placed among the most elite research universities in the country, we believe that our team at Ferdowsi University of Mashhad is well-positioned for this task. Objectives Our goal is to become an international scientific authority in soft computing and intelligent information processing by the following components Address the basic challenges of humanity by the tools of soft computing and intelligent information processing. Advance the state of the art on the worldwide theory of soft computing and intelligent information processing. Foster the recognition and advancement of the science of intelligent systems and knowledge engineering both nationally and internationally. Better introduce soft computing and intelligent information processing to the society and the industrial/academic experts Form national and international teams of academicians and industry experts to solve the basic challenges of humanity through the application of intelligent systems and knowledge engineering. Educate highly qualified experts in various related fields. Collaborate with various related industries for higher efficiency, improved design and better decisions. Help develop the required infrastructures for knowledge-based enterprises. What is soft computing: Soft computing is an umbrella term that covers the various integral paradigms of intelligent systems such as fuzzy logic, neural networks, along with other tools of intelligent information processing. Soft computing emphasizes the synergism among these paradigms of intelligence in solving the many open and difficult world problems of humanity today. Activities In its initial four years of operation, our members have published well over 600 journal articles and 460 conference papers; organized well over 40 conferences; started 12 new graduate programs in related areas, signed 5 partnership agreements with other organizations of mutual interests such as national scientific societies, other centers of excellence, and the Iran Meteorological Organization; held over 86 public speeches; advised over 210 thesis/dissertations; and supported modern facilities/equipment for 12 partner laboratories. We have now extended our center by an additional 19 national and international faculty partners in various fields of engineering, basic sciences, mathematics, and humanities. With the rapid and vast developments in science and technology in recent years, the need for specialized research-based activities in Iran has increasingly been realized. This issue and the need to enhance the scientific potentials in the country, that is, to reduce the research gap with the developed countries and to increase the cooperation between Iranian universities, the Department of Statistics at the Ferdowsi University of Mashhad managed to establish a specialized Center of Excellence in Statistics in 2005 in agreement with three other universities, i.e., Tarbiyat Modares, Isfahan, and Birjand universities. This led to the approval of the center by the Ministry of Science, Research and Technology. Therefore, in the second course, this center was titled “Ordered and Spatial Data Center of Excellence” and continued its activities for 5 years. To expand the activities, this center has also been cooperating with Tehran University and Razi University of Kermanshah as well as the above-mentioned universities in its third course. This cooperation is based on the regulations and conditions of the Centers of Excellence in Iran, which paves the way for further interactions among Iranian universities. In 2011, after evaluation and acceptance of the proposed programs for the creation of a specialized center of excellence by the Ministry of Science, Research and Technology, this center continued its activities for another 5 years in its third course by the same title of “Ordered and Spatial Data Center of Excellence”. The Ordered and Spatial Data Center of Excellence aims to achieve the following objectives: To promote and disseminate the science of statistics in Iran To develop international scientific relations Its main aim is to provide services in the country as well as in neighboring countries. The center also seeks to identify infectious and noninfectious factors leading to ruminant abortion and neonatal mortality in the Khorasan provinces. Another aim of the Center of Excellence in Ruminant Abortion and Neonatal Mortality is to identify the geographical distribution of this issue. During the last decade, a number of conferences have been organized in this field by the Ferdowsi University of Mashhad and other universities in Iran. A large number of Iranian and international researchers have attended such academic events. Members of this center have published a considerable number of research papers in the field of Analysis including Functional Analysis, Theory of Operators, Harmonic Analysis, Functional Equations, and also in the field of Algebra including Theory of Groups, Chains, Modules, and Homology. The Center of Excellence in Analysis on Algebraic Structures is attempting to achieve its aims through a range of activities and approaches such as extending the relationships between the two branches of Analysis on Algebraic Structures, i.e., Analysis and Algebraic, increasing scientific production contributing to knowledge, and developing a more dynamic environment for training talented students. Publishing significant scholarly papers by the members of this center helps the promotion of the scientific level of the country as well the region and the world. The Center of Excellence in Analysis on Algebraic Structures has the advantage of benefiting from the services of 3 Full Professors and 4 Associate Professors who have published many outstanding scientific products. The following activities occur at this scholarly center: Scientific production focusing on interdisciplinary fields Help in publishing scholarly journals in mathematics (as members of the editorial boards) Cooperation with international scientific associations (in the review of publications in Mathematics) Organizing national and international conferences and workshops and professional training courses Training future researchers through supervision of postgraduate students Providing scientific as well as financial support for talented students Cooperation with other universities in carrying out research projects Planning for running post-doctoral program The future plan of this center will be to establish an interdisciplinary branch on Analysis and Algebra. This center, which has been established in response to the global scientific need and to the future needs of this country, will be active with the collaboration between scientists in the country and abroad. Studies on master plan programming, design, and implementation can be categorized into 14 chapters: 1. Basic Studies; 2. Educational Programming; 3. Spatial- Physical Cognition; 4. University’s Buildings Identification; 5. Principles of University Spaces Design; 6. World Case Study; 7. Spatial Analysis of Campus Land uses; 8. Physical Programming Principles; 9. Campus Design Principles; 10. Transportation and Traffic; 11. Campus Signs; 12. Landscape and Environment; 13. Passive Defense; 14. Building and Construction Details. In recent years, Islamic countries have considered “Islamic traditions and Contemporary Design” as the principles of university's outlook. Due to the physical needs and value-oriented viewpoints, the physical outlook of Ferdowsi University of Mashhad can be determined as below: Development and improvement of the university’s spatial needs following the sustainable development of Iranian- Islamic architecture patterns. Environment improvement, resource conservation, and green university achievement have been noted as the main goal of physical programming. Design strategies can be categorized into the UI GreenMeteric WUR criteria: 1. Setting and Infrastructures; 2. Energy and Climate Changes; 3. Waste; 4. Water; 5. Transportation and 6. Education. The ambition for achieving these criteria led the design team to focus on reducing environmental damages and spreading the use of renewable energies and green technologies. The main goals of FUM are as follows: Increasing place attachment and creating a strong sense of place; Developing a scientific, healthy, and creative environment; Creating sociable environments and desirable interaction; Considering architecture, urban and environmental design criteria (to achieve a green campus); Relationship between internal learning environments and external society; Promoting the current situation; Increasing environment legibility; Education, research, and experience in a responsive environment; Sustainable campus as an urban-regional sign. According to mentioned goals, the design strategies in the campus master plan are: Relationship with the city; Consideration of Iranian-Islamic architecture patterns following contemporary design principles; Green architecture design; Campus walkways development; Creating linking buildings; Space optimization; Environmentally adaptive architecture; Use of the latest space standards Considering future universities' architectural principles; Creating social learning centers in 9 zones of the campus; Creating a legible spatial network over the campus; Use of on-site ecological potentials and renovation of the stream as the ecologic axis; To legible the 12 faculties' borders; To unify the same land uses and avoid diffused buildings over the campus; To create recreational and desirable environments for students and other users; Green light transportation system on the main axis of the campus; The Legible entrances for campus; Creating a socio-physical area in heart of the campus; To increase accessibility to different destinations over the campus; Maximum use of current buildings and renovating them; Minimum of destruction and maximum flexibility in future buildings; Respect for the physical-spatial history of the campus and reviving the memories; and To achieve 90 sqm public per capita and 27 sqm spatial per capita for each student. SARI is a market driven research institute in the field of renewable energies set to move towards creativity, innovation and marketplace. The vision of the institute is to become a leader in the field of renewable energies, whose portfolio, research agenda and research based educational model align with the shifting needs of a developed country. The mission of the institute involves research, design, manufacturing of prototypes and commercialization as well as empowering enthusiastic graduates and graduate students for entering into the world of innovation and entrepreneurship. SARI consists of three departments of wind energy, solar energy and energy storage. Current activities are mostly focused on the wind turbine design and related research projects. Improvement of organic polymer solar cells, ion lithium batteries and redox flow batteries are some of main research areas of the institute at the time. Since the city of Mashhad is geographically located near the North-East gas resources of the country and also close to the Shahid Hasheminejad Refinery Station, it has a strategic situation. On the other hand, benefiting from a wealth of knowledgeable faculty members and talented students, Ferdowsi University of Mashhad has shown its capacity and capability in implementing research projects and publishing research papers in different areas of oil and gas industries. Taking this background into consideration, the establishment of the Research Institute of Oil & Gas at Ferdowsi University of Mashhad provides a platform where the problems of these industries and Oil and Gas issues can be taken into considerations. Thus, this institute has the potential to be considered as one of the leading research centers for excellence. The Research Institute of Oil & Gas at Ferdowsi University of Mashhad is established to fulfill the aims of the Iranian government in promoting research centers. It has the ability of developing and improving technologies needed for oil and gas industries. The Research Institute of Oil and Gas creates added value by training human resources required by oil and gas industries and providing related jobs. This research center is capable of not only decreasing the scientific dependence of Iran on other countries but also exporting oil and gas technologies to other countries especially to neighboring countries. The new Theory of Wavelets and Wavelet Estimation Modules replaced classical theories including Classical Fourier Theory to solve different practical problems in Seismology, Signal Processing Systems, Telecommunications, Image Processing and Computer Vision, Elementary Particles, Theory of Approximation and Location, Forensic, Genetics and Medicine, Engineering, and Physics. Industrial centers and research laboratories try to apply the effective Wavelet Approximation Methods to enhance the quality of their products and the accuracy of their experiments. This new practical theory of Mathematics is the most effective link between Pure Mathematics and Applied Mathematics. The application of Wavelet Theory in industrial zones, universities, and high-tech laboratories like nano-technology labs can be a great help to a dramatic industrial progress in Iran. It can also solve the problems in different organizations of Iran such as telecommunications and seismology. In this regard, there is a need to educate and train experienced researchers. Establishing the Research Center for Wavelets Applications in Linear and Nonlinear Systems with the above-mentioned objectives is of significant importance to Iran. This center can be a place to conduct research projects and wavelet systems modeling as well as solving issues in Engineering, Medicine, Agriculture, Economy, Industry, Nuclear Energy, Telecommunications, and Computer Hardware and Software and providing proper solutions. It was extended to a ‌ B otany Research Department after a decade of activity, in 1991. In 2000, due to the research objectives of the University, the plan of developing department into a Research Center for Plant Sciences was ratified and the Center preceded its activities as an independent center with three research departments namely Botany, Legumes and Ornamental plants. Undoubtedly, this success has prompted the distinguished scholars of Iran to develop Islamic sciences and theories. Innovations and knowledge productions in Humanities, which highlights the role of religion in the education of people and managing the society, are the key factors which helped sustain the Islamic revolution. In this regard, the significant role of seminary and university potentials of Islamic countries including Iran cannot be ignored. Seminaries, as traditional and universities as modern scientific institutions are two important places that aim to educate scholars in Iran. It is also worth mentioning that there are very few cities in Iran in which there is a well-known university as well as a reputable seminary. The Holy city of Mashhad in Iran is one such city. The seminary of Mashhad (which due to the presence of Illuminated Imam Ali ibn Musa al-Reza (A.S.) and the Holly Shrine are well recognized) along with the Ferdowsi University of Mashhad have made this city a remarkable place where seminary and university are united and become centers for Islamic studies. In 2006, seminary and university professors, the Friday prayer leader of Mashhad, and the President of the Ferdowsi University of Mashhad arranged meetings in which important issues like the unity of seminary and university as well as the importance, aims, purposes and programs of this unitary were discussed. These meetings emphasized a new way of thinking in the realm of spiritual thought in Humanities. Considering the need for such studies in Iran, the Research Center for Islamic Studies in Humanities was established in 2001 by the virtue of an article number 16519/22 passed by the Ministry of Science, Research, and Technology on December 5, 2007. Aims To explain the research process in Humanities regarding Islamic ideas and theories To establish and increase the communication between university scholars and Islamic and Humanities centers To identify and study issues related to Islamic sciences and Humanities To welcome collaboration and cooperation with other national and international research centers and institutes to improve the quality of research on issues related to Islam and Humanities To conduct fundamental, practical, and developmental studies in each research department To identify different Islamic thoughts and propositions in Humanities and Social Sciences To open new horizons in research and studies, which are directly related to religion and Islamic society with the main focus on interdisciplinary ones. Departments: Islamic Economy, Islamic Management, Islamic Education, Jurisprudence and Islamic Law Missions Islamization of Humanities with regard to the potentials at Ferdowsi University of Mashhad and seminary of Mashhad Encouraging students of higher education to conduct interdisciplinary studies in Islamic sciences and Humanities Providing the proper conditions for theorizing in Islamic Humanities Identifying the research areas and gaps in Islamic Humanities Work towards Islamization of the humanities axis using the capacity of Ferdowsi University and Khorasan Seminary interaction Encourage postgraduate students to study and research in the field of interdisciplinary studies of Islamic and human sciences Trying to create a favorable environment in the field of Islamic human sciences theory Identifying Practical fields of Islamic humanities studies. Vision Research collaboration with educational or research institutions inside and outside of Iran to improve the quality of research activities in the fields of Islamic sciences and humanities Explain the research in principles of Humanities according to the Islamic viewpoints in order to achieve long-term goal to develop and research with Islamic perspectives in the field of humanities. The Management Research Center, established in 2006 at the Ferdowsi University of Mashhad, benefits from the services of many experienced and specialized researchers. The belief underlying the establishment of this research center is that sustainable and comprehensive development is possible only if activities of organizations and their managers are based on research findings. Knowledgeable professors and experienced experts at the Management Research Center are ready to collaborate in research projects of organizations and to consult in different management aspects such as strategies, organizational infrastructures, organizational culture, human resources, production, and marketing. Animal species are of great importance for interdisciplinary studies. Indeed, these species provide the possibility of several common research projects among different branches of biological science, fundamental science, Veterinary medicine, experimental medicine and agricultural science. Animal kingdom, as the largest and the most complex category of organisms, includes an important part of the genetic resources and biological diversity.  Consequently, animals have always played an important role in benchmarking and entrepreneurship. Iran, with its high climatic variation and different terrestrial and aquatic environments, has valuable genetic resources which can lead us to develop zoological-based technologies, and to elaborate innovations in bioproduction. Studies on master plan programming, design, and implementation can be categorized into 14 chapters: 1. Basic Studies; 2. Educational Programming; 3. Spatial- Physical Cognition; 4. University’s Buildings Identification; 5. Principles of University Spaces Design; 6. World Case Study; 7. Spatial Analysis of Campus Land uses; 8. Physical Programming Principles; 9. Campus Design Principles; 10. Transportation and Traffic; 11. Campus Signs; 12. Landscape and Environment; 13. Passive Defense; 14. Building and Construction Details. In recent years, Islamic countries have considered “Islamic traditions and Contemporary Design” as the principles of university's outlook. Due to the physical needs and value-oriented viewpoints, the physical outlook of Ferdowsi University of Mashhad can be determined as below: Development and improvement of the university’s spatial needs following the sustainable development of Iranian- Islamic architecture patterns. Environment improvement, resource conservation, and green university achievement have been noted as the main goal of physical programming. Design strategies can be categorized into the UI GreenMeteric WUR criteria: 1. Setting and Infrastructures; 2. Energy and Climate Changes; 3. Waste; 4. Water; 5. Transportation and 6. Education. The ambition for achieving these criteria led the design team to focus on reducing environmental damages and spreading the use of renewable energies and green technologies. The main goals of FUM are as follows: Increasing place attachment and creating a strong sense of place; Developing a scientific, healthy, and creative environment; Creating sociable environments and desirable interaction; Considering architecture, urban and environmental design criteria (to achieve a green campus); Relationship between internal learning environments and external society; Promoting the current situation; Increasing environment legibility; Education, research, and experience in a responsive environment; Sustainable campus as an urban-regional sign. According to mentioned goals, the design strategies in the campus master plan are: Relationship with the city; Consideration of Iranian-Islamic architecture patterns following contemporary design principles; Green architecture design; Campus walkways development; Creating linking buildings; Space optimization; Environmentally adaptive architecture; Use of the latest space standards Considering future universities' architectural principles; Creating social learning centers in 9 zones of the campus; Creating a legible spatial network over the campus; Use of on-site ecological potentials and renovation of the stream as the ecologic axis; To legible the 12 faculties' borders; To unify the same land uses and avoid diffused buildings over the campus; To create recreational and desirable environments for students and other users; Green light transportation system on the main axis of the campus; The Legible entrances for campus; Creating a socio-physical area in heart of the campus; To increase accessibility to different destinations over the campus; Maximum use of current buildings and renovating them; Minimum of destruction and maximum flexibility in future buildings; Respect for the physical-spatial history of the campus and reviving the memories; and To achieve 90 sqm public per capita and 27 sqm spatial per capita for each student. Finite fault and rupture processing modeling, study on earthquake hazards and Seismic tomography are some of the main interests at EQRC. An advanced permanent seismic broadband network (FUMSN) in Khorasan provinces installed and operated by EQRC, is one of the three important seismic networks in Iran. EQRC is planning to position itself in high end research and development in field of exploration geophysics as well adding two more research groups and rename itself to Institute of Geophysical Technology (IGT) in near future. Here are the long term targets of IGT: Planned purchase of 800 TFlops super-computer, IGT will support computing intensive processes such as reservoir simulation, geological modeling as well as heavy duty seismic imaging applications in near future. Recruitment of talented faculties in the field of geophysics, IGT has experienced faculty members with more than 10 years of experience in international Oil and Gas companies mainly in petroleum exploration.IGT is actively looking for team members to join us to better position itself in geophysical science in Iran. Partnering up with geophysical contractors, In addition of these, IGT is collaborating with seismic processing and interpretation companies as well as research institutes to secure some National Iranian Oil Company (NIOC) projects. Research on physics of the wave IGT is branching a new group called physics of the wave to dig deeper in the concept and mechanisms of the wave propagation in complicated mediums such as poro-viscoelastic and plastic mediums. Current Major Projects Expansion of portable and permanent broad band seismic network 800 Tflops GPU supercomputer, which can be used to perform heavy duty seismic processing applications and reservoir simulations Infrasonic Passive Differential Spectroscopy (IPDS), to detect passively (without using controlled source), the possibility of existence of a hydrocarbon reservoir Reverse time migration for better sub-surface imaging(approved by NIOC, waiting for contract) Research Facilities EQRC has a permanent broadband seismic network (FUMSN) in Khorasan provinces with 11 stations. This network provides high quality seismic data for all scientists who interested to study on earthquakes and earth sciences. Also EQRC is equipped to advanced portable seismometers for researches on special events in different parts of Iran. 12 channels surface seismic equipment (ABEM-MK8) is another facility at EQRC which make a good opportunity for graduate students to experience for near surface exploration. You may find a laboratory with shaking table, seismic wave and stick-slip fault simulators and high performance computer at EQRC. EQRC has 8 faculty members and is located in Ferdowsi university of Mashhad campus occupying around 1500 sqm of space. This office is responsible for providing suitable scientific and professional guidelines for the expansion and development of research and technology. Some of the duties of this department are policy making for research and technology, communicating with local and foreign universities, cooperating in providing scientific, cultural and social services by holding seminars and scientific conferences, publishing scientific findings and supervising all research affairs of the university, libraries and the university’s databases. The Vice-President for Research and Technology of the Ferdowsi University of Mashhad acts as the head of the University’s Research Council, the head of the Scientific Journals Council, the secretary of the University’s Scientific Poles Council, the head of the Policy Making Council for the University’s Research Centers, the secretary for the university network of deputies for research affairs and the country’s North-East research and technology associations. Research Council The Research Council is an association for preparing and developing research plans and regulations. This Council is also responsible for reviewing and approving of research proposals and the research activities of academic staff of the university. The members of this Council include: the Vice-President for Research and Technology, the Head for Research Affairs, the Head of Post-Graduate Studies, the Vice-President for Research, the  Research deputies of various facultys on campus and two members of academic staff having valuable research activities, recommended by the Vice-President for Research and Technology and approved by the University’s Research Council. Publications Committee The Publications Working Group has been established taking into consideration the development and implementation of plans and regulations of the University’s Press, approving the academic staffs’ books for publication and other book publishing advisors in the University’s publication series. This working group has been formed in the two permanent and faculty committee forms and the members of this working group are: the Vice-President for Research and Technology (as the committee head), the head of research affairs (the committee head), and the University’s head for the printing and publication association. The relevant faculty’s research deputy (based on the suggested publications), and two specialists in the related publication field (suggested by the secretary and the approval of the head of the committee). Technology Development Center The Technology Development Center of the Ferdowsi University of Mashhad was established in September 2004 by signing a partnership and with cooperation of the Khorasan Science and Technology Park. 28 companies are working in this complex at this time. This center is working in three places and under these titles: Center for Entrepreneurial Development (next to the Faculty of Natural Resources and Environment). Center for Technology Development (next to the Faculty of Engineering) (Incubator). Center for Comprehensive Technology Development (University east door – opposite to Kherad Park). Top

Faculty of Theology and Islamic Studies / Department of Islamic Philosophy and Theosophy Department of Islamic Philosophy and Theosophy The department of Islamic Philosophy and Theosophy was established in 1958 at the Ferdowsi University of Mashhad. In this department, the students become familiar with Islamic philosophy and methods of defying atheistic ideas. The alumni are specialized in Islamic sciences and will be able to overcome incertitude in faith issues. Moreover, B.A., M.A., and Ph.D. students graduating in this major are expected to be knowledgeable in the fields of logic and mysticism. Founded in 1975, the Master’s program for Philosophy and Theosophy aims to make students familiar with philosophical and divine issues in the Islamic as well as Western world. The aim of this program is to enhance students’ capabilities in defending the Islamic principles and ideology. The doctoral program has been admitting candidates since 2011. This program aims to help students to become knowledgeable about Mulla Sadra’s philosophical theory. Mulla Sadra or Mollasadra or Sadr-ol-Mote'allehin was an Iranian Shia Islamic philosopher, theologian and scholar who led the Iranian cultural renaissance in the 17th century. The objective of this kind of study is to empower doctoral candidates with the ability to employ such theories in social issue such as ethics, politics, education, etc. More Head of the Department of Islamic Philosophy and Theosophy Gahangir Masoudi Associate Professor Department of Islamic Philosophy and Theosophy masoudi-g@um.ac.ir +985138803860 Concentration areas offered by the Department of Islamic Philosophy and Theosophy Areas Bachelor's Master's Ph.D Theology and Islamic Studies-Islamic philosophy and Theosophy - Faculty of Theology and Islamic Studies / Department of Islamic Knowledge and Sciences Department of Islamic Knowledge and Sciences The Bachelor’s program of the Department of Islamic Knowledge and Sciences was established in 2004 to offering general courses in Islamic knowledge and sciences. The Master’s program established in 2006 aims at training students for teaching courses in Islamic knowledge and sciences at universities and also institutions of higher education in Iran and other countries. This program also focuses on strengthening and improving the educational and scientific levels of the applicants to teach courses in Islamic knowledge and sciences. The graduates of this program can further their studies in Islamic knowledge and sciences. Graduates are also capable of serving as researchers at academic and research centers to perform research on Islamic thought and knowledge or on subjects related to the subjects of their studies. Founded in 2006 at the Ferdowsi University of Mashhad, the doctoral program aims at preparing lecturer for teaching Islamic Knowledge and Sciences at institutions of higher education institutions in Iran and other countries. This department also aims at strengthening and improving the educational competences and scientific levels of the faculty members in universities in the departments of Islamic Knowledge and Sciences. The graduates of this program can participate in research activities of academic and research centers in the fields of religious thought and Islamic knowledge and in subject areas related to subjects offered in Islamic knowledge and sciences program. One of the objectives of the doctoral program of the Department of Islamic Knowledge and Science is promoting the rank of current faculty members who are lecturers now at Islamic Knowledge and Sciences departments of universities to Assistant Professor. Faculty of Theology and Islamic Studies / Department of Islamic Civilization and Culture Department of Islamic Civilization and Culture In 1969, the Department of Islamic Civilization and Culture was establish at the Faculty of Theology at the Ferdowsi University of Mashhad. Students in the Bachelor’s program are expected to develop knowledge of identifying and revitalizing resources of cultural heritage and to acknowledge the role of Iranians in the development of Islamic civilization. They are also expected to demonstrate ability to study the developmental factors as well as the obstacles in the development of Islamic civilization and to become familiar with historical geography of Islamic countries. The Department of Islamic Civilization and Culture offers Master’s program with the aim of preparing researchers in Islamic History and Arts and as a whole in different subject areas of Islamic civilization and culture. This department also trains specialists who can serve the needs of Cultural Offices and delegations of the Islamic Republic of Iran in other countries. The Department of Islamic Civilization and Culture expects graduates to be able to help the enhancement of scientific knowledge of officials and cultural specialists of governmental organizations. The Department of Islamic Civilization and Culture also offers a Doctoral program. The aim of this program is to prepare researchers as well as academics capable of teaching and carrying out research in universities and other educational institutions and specialists in Islamic studies. It also attempts to educate Islamic officials for Iranian offices and delegates in other countries. The well-equipped and large labs support teaching and research activities regarding large and small animals, theriogenology and reproductive diseases, surgery and anesthetics, radiology and sonography, and poultry and clinical pathology. The clinic is now a reference center for diagnosis and treatment of animals and poultry diseases in the region. To promote and develop its educational and research activities, the Department of Veterinary Clinical Sciences has established the Ph.D. programs for Small Animal Internal Medicine since 2002, D.V.Sc in 2010, and Clinical Pathology and Surgery since 2012. Studies on master plan programming, design, and implementation can be categorized into 14 chapters: 1. Basic Studies; 2. Educational Programming; 3. Spatial- Physical Cognition; 4. University’s Buildings Identification; 5. Principles of University Spaces Design; 6. World Case Study; 7. Spatial Analysis of Campus Land uses; 8. Physical Programming Principles; 9. Campus Design Principles; 10. Transportation and Traffic; 11. Campus Signs; 12. Landscape and Environment; 13. Passive Defense; 14. Building and Construction Details. In recent years, Islamic countries have considered “Islamic traditions and Contemporary Design” as the principles of university's outlook. Due to the physical needs and value-oriented viewpoints, the physical outlook of Ferdowsi University of Mashhad can be determined as below: Development and improvement of the university’s spatial needs following the sustainable development of Iranian- Islamic architecture patterns. Environment improvement, resource conservation, and green university achievement have been noted as the main goal of physical programming. Design strategies can be categorized into the UI GreenMeteric WUR criteria: 1. Setting and Infrastructures; 2. Energy and Climate Changes; 3. Waste; 4. Water; 5. Transportation and 6. Education. The ambition for achieving these criteria led the design team to focus on reducing environmental damages and spreading the use of renewable energies and green technologies. The main goals of FUM are as follows: Increasing place attachment and creating a strong sense of place; Developing a scientific, healthy, and creative environment; Creating sociable environments and desirable interaction; Considering architecture, urban and environmental design criteria (to achieve a green campus); Relationship between internal learning environments and external society; Promoting the current situation; Increasing environment legibility; Education, research, and experience in a responsive environment; Sustainable campus as an urban-regional sign. According to mentioned goals, the design strategies in the campus master plan are: Relationship with the city; Consideration of Iranian-Islamic architecture patterns following contemporary design principles; Green architecture design; Campus walkways development; Creating linking buildings; Space optimization; Environmentally adaptive architecture; Use of the latest space standards Considering future universities' architectural principles; Creating social learning centers in 9 zones of the campus; Creating a legible spatial network over the campus; Use of on-site ecological potentials and renovation of the stream as the ecologic axis; To legible the 12 faculties' borders; To unify the same land uses and avoid diffused buildings over the campus; To create recreational and desirable environments for students and other users; Green light transportation system on the main axis of the campus; The Legible entrances for campus; Creating a socio-physical area in heart of the campus; To increase accessibility to different destinations over the campus; Maximum use of current buildings and renovating them; Minimum of destruction and maximum flexibility in future buildings; Respect for the physical-spatial history of the campus and reviving the memories; and To achieve 90 sqm public per capita and 27 sqm spatial per capita for each student. Veterinary Medicine / Department of Pathobiology Department of Pathobiology The faculty members of the Department of Pathobiology are active in teaching and productive research in different subjects including Pathology, Immunology, Bacteriology and Bacterial Diseases, Virology and Viral Diseases, Mycology and Fungal Diseases, Parasitology and Parasitic Diseases, and Biotechnology. The well-equipped labs of this department support teaching and research activities in Immunology, Virology, Parasitology, Bacteriology, Mycology, and Cell Culture. In addition to teaching and research activities, this department supports laboratory services for the faculty’s clinic. For example, the Pathology section provides autopsy and histopathology. The Department of Pathobiology has been offering postgraduate programs such as a Ph.D. program for Biotechnology and Parasitology since 2007, a Master’s program for Parasitology since 2009, a Master’s program for Bacteriology since 2011, a Ph.D. program for Veterinary Pathology, and a Ph.D. program for Bacteriology since 2015. Veterinary Medicine / Department of Basic Science Department of Basic Sciences The Department of Basic Sciences at the Faculty of Veterinary Sciences benefits from a large number of academics who are active in teaching and productive in research in different fields such as Biochemistry Physiology, Pharmacology, Anatomy, Histology, Embryology, Genetics and Toxicology. The Fundamentals of structure and function of animals and human beings are comparatively studied in these fields from different perspectives such as microscopic and macroscopic, molecular, and cellular, histologic, and organismal biology. These courses provide theoretical and experimental foundations for learning physiology, different diseases, clinical and experimental courses. The Department of Basic Sciences has a number of laboratories for Biochemistry, Physiology, Pharmacology, Toxicology and Anatomy. These labs are used for teaching and research projects. Various types of research techniques are used in these labs. Based on its teaching and research capacities this department has started offering various postgraduate programs including the Ph.D. program for Comparative Histology since 2009, the Master’s program for Physiology since 2010, the Ph.D. program for Physiology, the Master’s program for Clinical Biochemistry since 2012, and the Master’s program for Histology since 2013. of Veterinary Medicine Faculty of Veterinary Medicine The Faculty of Veterinary Medicine was established in 1991. The aim of this faculty is to provide highly-skilled and expert human resources capable of carrying out research and providing health, treatment and research services in various branches of Veterinary Medicine. The initial educational programs of this faculty were: Doctor of Veterinary Medicine and Doctor of Veterinary Medicine (D.V.M). Each year a large number of students are admitted to the Faculty of Veterinary Medicine at three educational levels: Doctor of Philosophy (Ph. D.), D.V.M, and Master of Science (M.Sc.). The departments at the Faculty of Veterinary Medicine include: Basic Sciences, Pathobiology, Food Hygiene and Aquaculture, Veterinary Clinical Sciences. The Faculty of Veterinary Medicine benefits from a large number of highly productive academics carrying out research and educational activities. The results of their scientific activities have a useful impact on the development of science and technology in Iran. A few of these activities are as follows: Research, education and consultancy cooperation with many institutions and executive bodies including the Ministry of Agriculture, the Veterinary Regional Office, Razi Vaccine and Serum Research Institute, the Academic Center for Education, the Culture and Research Organization (Jihad Daneshgahi), and the University of Medical Sciences. Establishing a special animal hospital and polyclinic located 5 kilometers away from the university campus. Providing clinical and laboratory services in the polyclinic and special hospital. Such facilities include: The table tennis indoor court: Constructed in an area of 345 square meters in 2002, it is located near the Fajr dormitory no. 4. The Open playgrounds in the Faculty of Literature and Humanities: These facilities, built in 2005, include Volleyball, Football, Basketball, and Futsal grounds in an area of 2090 square meters. Sciences / Department of Motor Behavior and Sport Management Department of Motor Behavior and Sport Management The degree program in Motor Behavior, established in 2009, was promoted as an independent educational department in 2013. However, the program for Sport Management is not an independent department yet. That is why these two programs have formed one department. This department offers two degree programs at the M.S. and Ph.D levels. The aim of the Motor Behavior program, established in 2009, is to train experts in Motor Behavior capable of teaching, planning, implementing, supervising, and doing innovative research and action in academic and professional environments. The program for Sport Management aims to train students knowledgeable of the principles and foundations of sport management, gaining deep awareness and practical skills for the strategic management of sport sectors. Graduates are expected to gain knowledge about the processes of sports management and sport industry and be able to analyze the problems in sports organizations and institutions and find solutions for them. Another aim of this program is to train and provide faculty members for universities, professional sport institutions, researchers, leaders and managers for sport organizations in Iran. Movements Department of Exercise Physiology and Sport Injuries and Corrective Movements The degree program for Sport Physiology aims to upgrade student's theoretical and experimental knowledge in relation to the mechanism of different systems of the body such as: in-cellular organs, tissues, vascular system, nervous muscle system and endocrine glands when acting. In this program, students are trained to carry out research in sport sciences and related subjects such as improving the efficiency of athletes and non-athletes, rehabilitation of patients, and measuring the effects of exercises on the people’s health and performance of people. The aim of the program for Sport Injuries and Corrective Movements is to provide experts capable of improving the physical and mental health as well as motor activities of people through teaching, research, planning, and supervising. Such people include a range of patients having physical and mental problems, which make a gap between them and normal public health. This also includes people who are at risk of sport damages, people known as patients, disabled or weak with low physical, mental and behavioral abilities indicating that they have shortcomings in health norms. Sport Sciences, which was established in 1993 under the name of the Faculty of Physical Education, aims to train experts in Sport Sciences to fulfill the country’s desire to promote sports and physical education. In 2014 the name of the Faculty changed to the Faculty of Sport Sciences. The faculty offers three degree programs. The Bachelor of Physical Education and Sport Sciences with two specializations (educational areas of specializations) in Biological Sciences and in Human Sciences. The Master’s programs are offered by the Department of Motor Behavior and Sports Management and the Department of Exercise Physiology, Sport Injuries and Corrective Movements. The Ph.D. program is offered by the Department of Motor Behavior and Sports Management. Science / Department of Physics / The Observatory of the Faculty of Sciences The Observatory of  the Faculty of Sciences The Observatory of the Faculty of Sciences was established in 40s Shamsi by Dr. Mohammad Ali Saadat at Ferdowsi University of Mashhad. The Observatory activities well acknowledged in June 2004 with the live webcast of the transit of Venus against the Sun. Currently, the Observatory hold public visits for schools, educational institutes, universities, etc. The practical sections of Observational Astronomy courses are arranged in this Observatory. Pupils and students whose observational projects are approved by the Department of Physics of the Faculty of Sciences of Ferdowsi University of Mashhad can take advantage of the facilities of the Observatory as well. In order to observe and record the phenomena such as eclipses, transit of planets and the like, Observatory holds other observational programs (for public or specialists). Facilities The observatory consists of 8 and 14-inch Schmidt–Cassegrain reflecting Telescope, CCD Imaging Camera, Spectrograph. Top

Physics Department of Physics The Department of Physics in the Faculty of Science at the Ferdowsi University of Mashhad was founded in September 1962, as a joint 3-year program in Mathematics and Physics. Later on, it was separated from the Department of Mathematics as an independent 4-year program in 1965. The Department of Physics is dedicated to educate undergraduate and graduate students, and to convey the concepts and logic of the discipline to broader scientific and industrial communities. The students admitted to this program can study in either one of the following academic areas of specialization: Astronomy and astrophysics, Nuclear Physics, Elementary Particle Physics, Condensed matter physics and Geophysics. Currently, the department admits students at undergraduate, graduate, and postgraduate levels. Bachelor’s students can enroll in the undergraduate program of physics. However, graduate and postgraduate students choose one of the following programs. M.Sc. Chemistry Department of Chemistry The Department of Chemistry established its Bachelor’s program in 1965. At present it offers two undergraduate programs, i.e., Pure Chemistry and Applied Chemistry. The Department of Chemistry founded its Master’s program in 1997. In designing this program several factors such as deepening students’ understanding of chemical issues and their applications in fulfilling societal needs, developing students’ confidence and creativity in research, promoting their skills to enable them to act as an expert in the field to accomplish occupational tasks were taken into consideration. Currently, the students in the Masters’ program can study in one of the following areas of specialization: Organic Chemistry, Analytical Chemistry, Inorganic Chemistry, Physical Chemistry, Biochemistry and Polymer Chemistry. The Ph.D. Program, established in 2003, aims at training specialists in new and advanced research methods to solve scientific problems of the society and educating specialists. The department also tries its best to train graduates who will be productive academic staff at universities and institutes of higher education. This program offers five year programs in the following program: Organic Chemistry, Analytical Chemistry, Inorganic Chemistry, Physical Chemistry, and Biochemistry. Department of Biology was established in 1967. The aim of this department in the B.Sc. program is to acquaint students with the basics of Biology, different theories, and applications of Biology in other fields. The minimum duration of study is 7 semesters, i.e. 3.5 years. There are 136 credit hours offered in this program. The Department of Biology also offers Masters and Ph.D. programs. Currently, there are 8 areas of specialization (educational areas of specializations) offered at the M.Sc. level: Cell and Molecular Biology, Animal Physiology, Animal Biosystematics, Plant Systematic-Ecology, Plant Physiology, Microbiology, Microbial Biotechnology, Cell and Developmental Biology. At the Ph.D. program, students can choose Cell and Molecular Biology, Animal Physiology, Animal Biosystematics, Plant Ecology, or Plant Physiology to continue their education. Studies on master plan programming, design, and implementation can be categorized into 14 chapters: 1. Basic Studies; 2. Educational Programming; 3. Spatial- Physical Cognition; 4. University’s Buildings Identification; 5. Principles of University Spaces Design; 6. World Case Study; 7. Spatial Analysis of Campus Land uses; 8. Physical Programming Principles; 9. Campus Design Principles; 10. Transportation and Traffic; 11. Campus Signs; 12. Landscape and Environment; 13. Passive Defense; 14. Building and Construction Details. In recent years, Islamic countries have considered “Islamic traditions and Contemporary Design” as the principles of university's outlook. Due to the physical needs and value-oriented viewpoints, the physical outlook of Ferdowsi University of Mashhad can be determined as below: Development and improvement of the university’s spatial needs following the sustainable development of Iranian- Islamic architecture patterns. Environment improvement, resource conservation, and green university achievement have been noted as the main goal of physical programming. Design strategies can be categorized into the UI GreenMeteric WUR criteria: 1. Setting and Infrastructures; 2. Energy and Climate Changes; 3. Waste; 4. Water; 5. Transportation and 6. Education. The ambition for achieving these criteria led the design team to focus on reducing environmental damages and spreading the use of renewable energies and green technologies. The main goals of FUM are as follows: Increasing place attachment and creating a strong sense of place; Developing a scientific, healthy, and creative environment; Creating sociable environments and desirable interaction; Considering architecture, urban and environmental design criteria (to achieve a green campus); Relationship between internal learning environments and external society; Promoting the current situation; Increasing environment legibility; Education, research, and experience in a responsive environment; Sustainable campus as an urban-regional sign. According to mentioned goals, the design strategies in the campus master plan are: Relationship with the city; Consideration of Iranian-Islamic architecture patterns following contemporary design principles; Green architecture design; Campus walkways development; Creating linking buildings; Space optimization; Environmentally adaptive architecture; Use of the latest space standards Considering future universities' architectural principles; Creating social learning centers in 9 zones of the campus; Creating a legible spatial network over the campus; Use of on-site ecological potentials and renovation of the stream as the ecologic axis; To legible the 12 faculties' borders; To unify the same land uses and avoid diffused buildings over the campus; To create recreational and desirable environments for students and other users; Green light transportation system on the main axis of the campus; The Legible entrances for campus; Creating a socio-physical area in heart of the campus; To increase accessibility to different destinations over the campus; Maximum use of current buildings and renovating them; Minimum of destruction and maximum flexibility in future buildings; Respect for the physical-spatial history of the campus and reviving the memories; and To achieve 90 sqm public per capita and 27 sqm spatial per capita for each student. Science Faculty of Science The Faculty of Science was established at the Ferdowsi University of Mashhad in 1961. This faculty now comprises of four departments including Geology, Biology, Chemistry, and Physics. The Faculty of Science has more than 2,000 students and more than half of them are postgraduate students. Research activities and scientific productions of the faculty members are of high standards and values in terms of quality and international reputation. As its major aims the Faculty of Sciences attempts to improve the quality of educational and research environment of the faculty, employ expert and experienced faculty members, launch new areas of specialization in postgraduate programs, publish authoritative specialized journals, improve the scientific papers of the faculty members as well as students in terms of quality and quantity, and cooperate with other universities and organization in performing research projects. Management Department of Range and Watershed Management The aim of the bachelor’s program for the Range and Watershed Management, established in 2005, is to train experts capable of managing range and watershed areas in Iran and overseas. This is due to the country’s increasing need for protein resources. Moreover, since the economic conditions of villagers and nomads are in direct relation to rangelands, we need experts who will be able to use local experiences as well as scientific findings and modern technologies to manage the country’s rangelands. They should also be able to take the principles of sustainable development into consideration, to protect major soil and water resources, and to manage the improvement of forage production and multiple uses of rangelands. Furthermore, events such as destructive floods and sever soil erosion which are the results of misuse of resources require systematic and comprehensive management of available local resources. The close interaction of students with natural environments is one of the outstanding characteristics and attractions of this field. During their studies, students will visit mountains, deserts and semi-desert areas in and out of the Khorasan Province. Students of Rangeland and Watershed Management receive necessary education in relation to the principles of soil and water protection. After graduation they will be able to do managerial and executive projects in watershed areas, prevention of floods and soil erosion. Local offices of natural resources, forestry and rangeland organizations, research institutions, universities and consulting engineering companies are among those institutions which can recruit and benefit from the graduates of Range and Watershed Management program.  More Head of the Department of Range and Watershed Management Abolfazl Mosaedi Professor Department of Range and Watershed Management mosaedi@um.ac.ir +9858805464 Concentration areas offered by the Department of Range and Watershed Management Areas Bachelor's Master's Ph.D Rang and Watershed Management - - Rangeland Management - - Watershed Management - - Academic staff Mahmood Azari Assistant Professor Email: Homepage: http://m.azari.profcms.um.ac.ir Mohammad Taghi Dastorani Professor Email: Homepage: http://dastorani.profcms.um.ac.ir Mohammad Farzam Professor Email: Homepage: http://mjankju.profcms.um.ac.ir Ali Golkarian Assistant Professor Email: Homepage: http://golkarian.profcms.um.ac.ir Mahdi Kolahi Assistant Professor Email: Homepage: http://mahdikolahi.profcms.um.ac.ir Kamal Naseri Associate Professor Email: Homepage: http://klnaseri.profcms.um.ac.ir Research Recent journal articles Ejtehadi, H., & Farzam, M. and Environment / Department of Desert Arid Zones Management Department of Desert Arid Zones Management The Department of Desert and Arid Zones Management (DAM) started its activities in 2005. The department has a mandate to carry out both teaching and research to address the problems of land degradation, with special emphasis on problems of wind erosion, desertification and proper management of natural resources of desert and arid regions of the country. The department offers high quality education to both undergraduate and postgraduate students with different courses which cover all aspects of arid zone management. The department’s mission is to train experts who have full knowledge about the limitations and potentials of deserts and can play significant roles in management of arid zones. Training these experts, therefore, helps prevent desertification, soil erosion and land degradation, exploit natural resources in arid and desert conditions, and control of people immigration from arid and semi-arid region. Major Objectives of the Department To impart higher education at undergraduate and post-graduate levels in the field of Desert and Arid Zones Management To supervise post-graduate students in planning, conducting, and evaluating students’ theses as part of their degree programs To develop closer link in line with departments and research organizations for mutual collaboration in research/development activities on natural resource conservation and improvements in deserts and arid zones of Iran To promote awareness among students, researchers, policy makers and the society in general about natural resource conservation and management through publishing articles and organizing seminars/workshops on the subjects related to natural resource management More Head of the Department of Desert Arid Zones Management Omid Safari Associate Prof. Department of Environmental Science Omid_Safari@yahoo.com +985138805451 Concentration areas offered by the Department of Desert Arid Zones Management Areas Bachelor's Master's Ph.D Desert Arid Zones - - Desert Zones Management - - Academic staff Morteza Akbari Assistant Professor Email: Homepage: http://m-akbari.profcms.um.ac.ir Alireza Rashki Associate Professor Email: Homepage: http://a.rashki.profcms.um.ac.ir Adel Sepehr Associate Professor Email: Homepage: http://adelsepehr.profcms.um.ac.ir Research Recent journal articles Shahsavari, A., Karimi, A., Akbari, M. Department of Fishery Sciences The Department of Fishery Sciences started its activities in 2012. Its major aim is to train experts in different branches of fisheries. Regarding the rapid growth of population in Iran and the limited food produced from natural resources, the aquaculture is taken into account in recent decades as an important food industry. The importance of food production, issues related to food security and people's interest in organic products shifts the society’s attentions to fishery industry as an important civil defense strategies. The production of farmed fisheries such as fish (warm water, cold water, cool water), crustaceans (shrimps, prawns, crayfishes, lobsters), clams (oysters), and reptiles (crocodiles) from an industrial point of view and ornamental fishes (from the recreational point of view) on one hand and the production of foods and food-medicines and even cosmetics (produced from unicellular algae) on the other hand have all made this educational program a very attractive one. Graduates from our Bachelor’s degree can continue their education in four educational areas of specialization such as Reproduction and Culture of Aquatic Species, Ecology of Fisheries, Processing of Fishery Products, and Fishing and Aquaculture Exploitation. The areas of specialization in Reproduction and Culture of Fisheries covers topics such as feeding of different fish and rearing systems using special designs (open, semi-open, and closed circuit). The focus on Aquatic Ecology covers subjects such as the study of Aquatic Behaviors, Preservation and Protection of Aquatics as well as establishing a Genetic Bank. Faculties and Departments / Faculty of Natural Resources and Environment / Department of Environmental Science Department of Environmental Science The Bachelor’s program for Environment Management was established to train experts in different branches of Environmental Sciences. The term environment has a broad range covering different subjects and components of nature and human environment. The imbalanced development of technologies and economics in modern times has brought us serious problems for the future of human beings and other species in the universe. At the global level, problems such as climate change and its consequences, decrease in biodiversity, decrease in fresh water resources, widespread pollution of water, air, soil, and foods all are challenging our lives. At the national level, the widespread destruction of natural resources, widespread pollution, destructive floods, extinction of valuable species of plants and animals all have led to deep concerns. Most of these problems stem from public ignorance, lack of professional human resources, and lack of local knowledge about environmental protection. The bachelor’s degree programs for Environmental Sciences attempts to develop skills in students in issues related to Environmental Sciences and also improve their abilities to implement projects related to such problems and provide solutions in line with sustainable development. Organizations and public institutions such as the Organization for Environmental Protection, local environment offices, local offices for natural resources, research institutions, municipalities, and consulting engineering companies are among those organizations who can recruit the graduates of the environmental sciences programs. During the four-year undergraduate program, students at the department of statistics can gain the skills for inferring, modeling and analyzing various economic and social systems. This undergraduate program also prepares the students to further their education. Graduates of this department will have the chance of being employed by both public and private sectors. The Master’s program in statistics was founded in 1987. The aim of this program is to educate specialists capable of teaching statistics and conducting research at universities and institutions of higher education as well as making a contribution to the management and planning of industrial centers and services such as Management and Planning Organization (MPO) and Statistical Center of Iran. The areas of specialization in the Master’s program of Statistics are Mathematical Statistics (since 1987) and Socio-Economic Statistics (since 2009).
